 * 
 * Represents site administrators who have full access for platform management, policy enforcement, user control, and official dispute handling. Maintains 3NF normalization by only holding role-specific identity, inheriting account details via shared foreign key references in actual system (e.g., via member or user account tables in other domains). For example, admins may be mapped to existing accounts for login. 
 * 
 * Key relationships: Not directly referencing other components to avoid duplication, but will use external user/member tables for ID in full implementation. 
 * Special behaviors: Only users elevated to this table have admin permissions; removal here revokes all admin rights.

 * 
 * Represents users with moderation powers: content review, temporary suspensions, and community management, without full admin rights. 3NF compliance is achieved by separating moderator role assignments from general user/member identity, with actual references made to external user/member accounts for linkage. 
 * 
 * Key relationships: In a full system, would reference members/users for role mapping. 
 * Special behaviors: Inclusion grants moderation rights; records are auditable for community trust and escalation protocols.
 * 
 * @namespace Actors
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe

export type discussionboard_moderators = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$discussionboard_moderatorsPayload>
/**

 * Member Role Model - Implements core registered user account role as specified in '02_discussionboard_user_roles_and_authentication.md'. 
 * 
 * Represents all authenticated users authorized to create content, interact, and participate in member-only features. Complies with 3NF by storing only role/enrollment information; user profile, security, and credentials exist in separate tables/domains. For example, email/username/password managed elsewhere but ID assigned here upon registration completion.
 * 
 * Key relationships: Mapped to outer user or authentication entity in wider system. 
 * Special behaviors: Granting/removing a row in this table assigns permission to create threads, participate in polls, etc.
 * 
 * @namespace Actors
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe

export type discussionboard_members = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$discussionboard_membersPayload>
/**
 * Model discussionboard_guests
 * Guest Role Model - Implements the guest browsing entity from '02_discussionboard_user_roles_and_authentication.md'. 
 * 
 * Represents unauthenticated and optionally semi-tracked users who may browse public content but not post/interact. Maintains 3NF as a distinct normalized table to assign and trace guest viewing sessions, apply access controls, and support future conversion (upgrade to member). For example, may store guest session or visitor tokens mapped to analytics.
 * 
 * Key relationships: May relate to external analytics/logs for guest tracking in broader system. 
 * Special behaviors: Deleting a guest here does not affect any member/admin records, ensuring normalization between roles.
 * 
 * @namespace Actors
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe

export type discussionboard_guests = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$discussionboard_guestsPayload>
/**
 * Model discussionboard_auth_sessions
 * Authentication Session Model - Implements the authentication and session tracking requirement from '02_discussionboard_user_roles_and_authentication.md' and ties policies in '05_discussionboard_business_rules_and_policies.md' (account locking, session expiry, etc.). 
 * 
 * Tracks active user/member sessions for login management, enforcing security policies, session timeouts, and role mapping. Complies with 3NF by separating session management from user identity, allowing independent lifecycle. For example, on login, a new row is created; on logout or expiry, row is ended.
 * 
 * Key relationships: Would reference user/member/role tables for session ownership in a full system.

export type discussionboard_auth_sessions = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$discussionboard_auth_sessionsPayload>
/**
 * Model discussionboard_threads
 * Thread Root Entity - This implements the 'thread management and creation' requirement from the features and user journeys documentation. Each instance represents an individual discussion thread (topic) started by a member, with links to category/section and root post. Maintains 3NF compliance by separating main thread data (title, status, author/member, section/category) from posts, histories, and related engagement. For example, a new thread '2025 Elections Discussion' would have one record here and many related post/comment records elsewhere. 
 * Key relationships: Links to author member, category, and root post via foreign keys. Special behaviors: Soft-deletion (archived flag), per-thread lock/pin status for moderation/admins.

 * @namespace ThreadsPosts

export type discussionboard_threads = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$discussionboard_threadsPayload>
/**
 * Model discussionboard_posts
 * Thread Post Entity - Implements the 'thread and comment posting', 'reply', and 'content moderation/reporting' features. Each represents an individual post or comment in a thread, with parent-child relation for comments (nested structure). Maintains 3NF compliance by keeping each post atomic and referring to its thread, author, and parent. For example, a threaded reply is a record here with a parent post. Key relationships: thread linkage, post author (member), optional parent for comments. Special behaviors: supports nested replies, soft deletion.

Each record is a snapshot of a post's content and metadata before or after an edit/action, maintaining a complete audit trail. Ensures 3NF by storing versions separately. For example, if a post is edited three times, there are three snapshot entries linked to the post. Key relationships: belongs to post, links to member who performed the edit/action. Special rules: records must not be deletable by regular users, only by admin/audit purge.

export type discussionboard_post_histories = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$discussionboard_post_historiesPayload>

 * Post Edit Log Entity - Implements granular audit-purposed logging for all post edits, satisfying compliance and traceability requirements beyond typical edit history. Each entry records who, when, and what change occurred, for every modification to any post. Maintains 3NF as every field relates directly to the primary key. For example, if a user performs three edits, all are logged here for admins/audits. Key relationships: links to post, edit-performing member.
 * 
 * @namespace ThreadsPosts
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type discussionboard_post_edit_logs = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$discussionboard_post_edit_logsPayload>
/**

Key relationships: links to thread, admin/mod who performed archival. Special behavior: archival should not delete thread/posts. Maintains 3NF.

 * @namespace ThreadsPosts
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe

export type discussionboard_thread_archives = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$discussionboard_thread_archivesPayload>

For example, when a member reports a post they believe is a violation, a new row is created here and linked to the moderation review process.

Maintains 3NF by linking actions to actors (moderator/admin), target content or users, and report IDs if applicable. E.g., When a moderator deletes a post for policy violation, this logs the event with details.

 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe

/**
 * Model discussionboard_post_likes

 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe

 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe

/**

 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */

/**

### `discussionboard_categories`

Discussion board categories - Implements categorization as specified in the requirements analysis section regarding navigability, content organization, and moderation targeting. This model supports organized user experience and functional requirements for thread placement, filtering, and role-based content management. Maintains 3NF by keeping category metadata atomic, without duplicating section or configuration data. For example, a member starts a thread under the 'Economics' category, which is mapped here for retrieval. Key relationships: references to discussionboard_sections (for section grouping) and possible linkage to threads (managed in another component). Special behaviors: categories can be disabled or reordered without affecting thread data.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each category, supporting distributed system architecture and audit trailing.
- `discussionboard_section_id`: Parent section's [discussionboard_sections.id](#discussionboard_sections) - Implements hierarchical grouping as per business requirements, enabling categories to be nested within sections for enhanced organization.
- `name`: Category name - Implements the display and search requirement for category labeling. Ensures normalization by isolating the label as atomic data. For example, 'Politics', 'Economics', 'International' etc.
- `description`: Category description - Provides contextual information to users and moderators. Maintains normalization by keeping explanations independent of other data. For instance, 'High-level discussions of macroeconomic issues.'
- `order`: Category display order - Controls sequence in UI navigation and listings. Maintains 3NF as it's not derived or duplicated from any other data. For example, '1' = top position on board.
- `enabled`: Is category enabled - Implements business rule for soft-hiding or disabling a category without deleting its record. Used in admin flows to turn categories on/off. For example, admins can disable a category temporarily during moderation.

### `discussionboard_sections`

Discussion board sections - Implements section-level grouping as per requirements covering board segmentation, navigation, and high-level access control. This entity solves the business need for upper-level organization beneath which categories (and subsequently threads) are grouped, supporting both frontend navigation and backend moderation targeting. Fully 3NF: atomic section label, description, and configuration linkage. For example, a section named 'Global Politics' groups multiple categories. Key relationships: can be referenced by categories and linked to board-wide configuration. Special behaviors: sections can be archived, reordered, or locked for content submission by toggling their enabled state.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each section, supporting scalable, distributed storage and system traceability.
- `discussionboard_configuration_id`: Configuration link [discussionboard_configurations.id](#discussionboard_configurations) - Associates the section with platform configuration for access control or behavior settings as per business policy.
- `name`: Section name - Implements navigation and search requirements for board-level organization. Normalized as atomic data. For example, 'Domestic Affairs', 'International Relations'.
- `description`: Section description - Context for users about the topical intent or rules. Fully normalized; avoids data redundancy. For instance, 'Contains threads related to domestic economic policy.'
- `order`: Section display order - Determines appearance in navigation and configuration panels. For example, order '0' = top section. 3NF: not dependent on non-key fields.
- `enabled`: Is section enabled - Controls visibility and posting capability for the section. Provides admin tools for platform segmentation as required by business rules.

### `discussionboard_configurations`

Discussion board configurations - Implements board-wide or section-specific settings, as required by platform policy and business rules for extensibility, permissions, and behavior customization. This model addresses operational flexibility: toggling feature flags, adjusting settings without schema changes, and supporting future platform growth. Maintains strict normalization: each configuration record atomic. For example, holding JSON settings for poll behaviors, default moderation options, or feature enablement. Key relationships: referenced by discussionboard_sections and possibly others in the future. Special behaviors: changes are audit-logged elsewhere; configurations are never deleted outright—only updated or replaced.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each configuration, supporting distributed storage and reliable referencing by other entities.
- `name`: Configuration name/key - Used for identification in admin tools and code. Normalized primary config label. Example: 'default_section_policy', 'poll_settings'.
- `settings_json`: Serialized configuration JSON - Stores all behavioral settings as a JSON string. Normalized: each config in its own row. For example, '{"allow_polls": true, "max_poll_options": 10}'
- `description`: Human-readable descriptive text about the configuration's purpose. Maintains normalization. For instance, 'Settings controlling default behaviors for domestic threads.'

### `discussionboard_admins`

Admin Role Model - This implements the administrative user role specification from '02_discussionboard_user_roles_and_authentication.md'. 

Represents site administrators who have full access for platform management, policy enforcement, user control, and official dispute handling. Maintains 3NF normalization by only holding role-specific identity, inheriting account details via shared foreign key references in actual system (e.g., via member or user account tables in other domains). For example, admins may be mapped to existing accounts for login. 

Key relationships: Not directly referencing other components to avoid duplication, but will use external user/member tables for ID in full implementation. 
Special behaviors: Only users elevated to this table have admin permissions; removal here revokes all admin rights.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique admin role identifier.
- `created_at`: Role assignment timestamp - Implements the auditability requirement. Records when the admin privilege was granted. Ensures temporal traceability for permission changes, supporting snapshot patterns by explicitly separating the assignment history. For example, when new admins are added, this field logs the event.

### `discussionboard_moderators`

Moderator Role Model - This implements the moderator role specification from '02_discussionboard_user_roles_and_authentication.md'. 

Represents users with moderation powers: content review, temporary suspensions, and community management, without full admin rights. 3NF compliance is achieved by separating moderator role assignments from general user/member identity, with actual references made to external user/member accounts for linkage. 

Key relationships: In a full system, would reference members/users for role mapping. 
Special behaviors: Inclusion grants moderation rights; records are auditable for community trust and escalation protocols.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique moderator role identifier.
- `created_at`: Role assignment timestamp - Tracks when the moderator privilege was activated. Supports audit trails and historical analysis of role distribution and trust elevation. For example, elevated by senior admins or via governance process.

### `discussionboard_members`

Member Role Model - Implements core registered user account role as specified in '02_discussionboard_user_roles_and_authentication.md'. 

Represents all authenticated users authorized to create content, interact, and participate in member-only features. Complies with 3NF by storing only role/enrollment information; user profile, security, and credentials exist in separate tables/domains. For example, email/username/password managed elsewhere but ID assigned here upon registration completion.

Key relationships: Mapped to outer user or authentication entity in wider system. 
Special behaviors: Granting/removing a row in this table assigns permission to create threads, participate in polls, etc.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique member role identifier.
- `created_at`: Role assignment timestamp - Logged at registration or membership upgrade. Used for eligibility/rule tracking and supports audit trails. For example, new signups receive this timestamp.

### `discussionboard_guests`

Guest Role Model - Implements the guest browsing entity from '02_discussionboard_user_roles_and_authentication.md'. 

Represents unauthenticated and optionally semi-tracked users who may browse public content but not post/interact. Maintains 3NF as a distinct normalized table to assign and trace guest viewing sessions, apply access controls, and support future conversion (upgrade to member). For example, may store guest session or visitor tokens mapped to analytics.

Key relationships: May relate to external analytics/logs for guest tracking in broader system. 
Special behaviors: Deleting a guest here does not affect any member/admin records, ensuring normalization between roles.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique guest identifier, e.g., guest session or pseudonymous token.
- `created_at`: Guest session/browsing assignment timestamp - Set when a guest session is first tracked or created. Used for analysis, conversion tracking to members, and policy enforcement (e.g., access window).

### `discussionboard_auth_sessions`

Authentication Session Model - Implements the authentication and session tracking requirement from '02_discussionboard_user_roles_and_authentication.md' and ties policies in '05_discussionboard_business_rules_and_policies.md' (account locking, session expiry, etc.). 

Tracks active user/member sessions for login management, enforcing security policies, session timeouts, and role mapping. Complies with 3NF by separating session management from user identity, allowing independent lifecycle. For example, on login, a new row is created; on logout or expiry, row is ended.

Key relationships: Would reference user/member/role tables for session ownership in a full system.
Special behaviors: Supports device/session concurrency policies, auditing of all critical actions (policy: audit trail for edits, deletions, moderation decisions).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique session identifier.
- `actor_type`: Role type associated with the session. Implements session role typing for permission checks (e.g., 'admin', 'moderator', 'member', 'guest'). Ensures normalization by separating session against role tables. For example: 'member' session tracks a logged in member, 'guest' for unauthenticated visitor.
- `actor_id`: Associated actor id (admin/member/moderator/guest). Implements role linking for session ownership. Ensures normalization so that user/role are tracked externally, this is a foreign key reference in broader system. For example, points to the 'id' of the corresponding role table depending on actor_type.
- `issued_at`: Session start timestamp. Implements session record creation for login audit trails. For example, set when user completes login.
- `expires_at`: Session expiration timestamp - Used to implement session expiry, security policy on inactivity, or explicit logout. For example, calculated by security policy or upon logout event.
- `last_activity_at`: Timestamp of the last activity on this session. Implements last-used tracking for security checks (token expiration, forced logout). For example, updated on each page load or action.
- `revoked_at`: Time at which session was revoked, if applicable. Implements security and forced logout. For example, set if session is invalidated by admin or system.
- `ip_address`: IP address recorded when session was initiated. Provides security auditing for login source and supports fraud monitoring. For example, '192.168.1.1'.
- `user_agent`: User agent string recorded on session establishment. Implements browser/device tracking policy for audit and security. For example, 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10...)'.

### `discussionboard_threads`

Thread Root Entity - This implements the 'thread management and creation' requirement from the features and user journeys documentation. Each instance represents an individual discussion thread (topic) started by a member, with links to category/section and root post. Maintains 3NF compliance by separating main thread data (title, status, author/member, section/category) from posts, histories, and related engagement. For example, a new thread '2025 Elections Discussion' would have one record here and many related post/comment records elsewhere. 
Key relationships: Links to author member, category, and root post via foreign keys. Special behaviors: Soft-deletion (archived flag), per-thread lock/pin status for moderation/admins.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique thread identifier.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Thread author's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). Refers to the member who created the thread.
- `discussionboard_category_id`: Thread's assigned [discussionboard_categories.id](#discussionboard_categories). Refers to the topic/category under which this thread is created.
- `title`: Thread title - Implements the required summary/title as per requirements document. Atomic, and always present. For example: '2025 Economic Outlook'.
- `status`: Thread status - Active, archived, locked. Implements moderation control requirement. For example: 'active', 'locked', 'archived'.
- `is_pinned`: Pinned flag - Whether this thread is pinned at the top. Implements thread management feature for moderators/admins. true if pinned by moderation.
- `is_locked`: Locked flag - Whether this thread is locked. Implements moderation tool for controlling participation. true if thread no longer accepts replies.
- `archived`: Soft delete/archive flag. If true, thread is hidden from public but data is retained for admins/audit. Implements audit/compliance rules.
- `created_at`: Thread creation timestamp. For audit/logging as per business rules.
- `updated_at`: Thread last updated timestamp. Updated on edits or moderation events. Required for audit trail and UX.

### `discussionboard_posts`

Thread Post Entity - Implements the 'thread and comment posting', 'reply', and 'content moderation/reporting' features. Each represents an individual post or comment in a thread, with parent-child relation for comments (nested structure). Maintains 3NF compliance by keeping each post atomic and referring to its thread, author, and parent. For example, a threaded reply is a record here with a parent post. Key relationships: thread linkage, post author (member), optional parent for comments. Special behaviors: supports nested replies, soft deletion.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique post identifier.
- `discussionboard_thread_id`: Referenced thread's [discussionboard_threads.id](#discussionboard_threads). Indicates which thread this post belongs to.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Author member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). Refers to the member who wrote this post or comment.
- `parent_post_id`: Optional parent [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts) (for replies/comments). Null for root posts; non-null for comments/replies to other posts.
- `body`: Post content body. Implements textual content storage. Fully normalized. For example: 'I think the economic forecast is optimistic.'
- `is_edited`: Edit flag. True if post has been edited after initial creation. Implements edit tracking policy.
- `is_deleted`: Soft delete flag. True if post is hidden from general users, retained for moderation/audit. Implements compliance and moderation rules.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of post creation. For chronology, moderation review, and user display.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last update. Reflects edit or moderation action.

### `discussionboard_post_histories`

Post History Snapshot Entity - Implements post edit/version control requirement. Each record is a snapshot of a post's content and metadata before or after an edit/action, maintaining a complete audit trail. Ensures 3NF by storing versions separately. For example, if a post is edited three times, there are three snapshot entries linked to the post. Key relationships: belongs to post, links to member who performed the edit/action. Special rules: records must not be deletable by regular users, only by admin/audit purge.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique snapshot record identifier.
- `discussionboard_post_id`: Target post's [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts). Indicates which post this snapshot is for.
- `edit_member_id`: Member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members) who performed the edit/action. For tracking responsible user.
- `old_body`: Prior post body (before edit/action). Implements versioned content requirement. Null if post was created (not edited yet).
- `new_body`: Edited (new) post body. Required for post change logs. Null if snapshot is for deletion (not rewording).
- `edit_type`: Type of edit/action (e.g., 'edit', 'delete', 'restore'). For audit and moderation policy linkage. For example: 'edit', 'delete'.
- `edit_reason`: Reason/comment for the edit, as recorded by the member or moderator. For moderation transparency, compliance.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this history/snapshot record was created. Fully normalized.

### `discussionboard_post_edit_logs`

Post Edit Log Entity - Implements granular audit-purposed logging for all post edits, satisfying compliance and traceability requirements beyond typical edit history. Each entry records who, when, and what change occurred, for every modification to any post. Maintains 3NF as every field relates directly to the primary key. For example, if a user performs three edits, all are logged here for admins/audits. Key relationships: links to post, edit-performing member.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique edit log record identifier.
- `discussionboard_post_id`: Edited post's [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts).
- `edit_member_id`: Editing member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members).
- `change_summary`: Brief summary of the edit. For quick audit purposes. Example: 'Fixed typo', 'Added reference'.
- `change_details`: Detailed information about the change (could be JSON or text). For investigation and compliance. Example: '{"from":"draft version","to":"final version"}'.
- `created_at`: Edit timestamp. For chronology.

### `discussionboard_thread_archives`

Thread Archive Entity - Implements thread archival/inactivation feature (from user cases/policies) whereby entire threads are hidden from public view on closure or due to compliance policy. This normalized entity stores archive records with references to thread, member (initiator), and reason. Example: a thread archived due to policy contains record here. Key relationships: links to thread, admin/mod who performed archival. Special behavior: archival should not delete thread/posts. Maintains 3NF.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique archive record identifier.
- `discussionboard_thread_id`: Thread's [discussionboard_threads.id](#discussionboard_threads) being archived.
- `archived_by_member_id`: Member (admin/moderator) [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members) who performed the archival.
- `archive_reason`: Reason/archive comment per moderation/audit policy implementation. Example: 'Thread closed for being off-topic.'
- `created_at`: Archival timestamp.

### `discussionboard_content_reports`

Content Report Entity - This implements the requirement for capturing and tracking user-reported content as defined in 'Business Rules and Policies' and across 'Features and Functional Specifications'.

This model records when a member or guest files a report on a post, comment, or thread for policy violations, harassment, or inappropriate content. It maintains normalized structure (3NF) by capturing report details and referencing the post/content in violation, along with the reporting user and reason. For example, when a member reports a post they believe is a violation, a new row is created here and linked to the moderation review process.

Key relationships: References reporter (member or guest by user_id/actor_id) and the offending content (from the threads/posts tables in the ThreadsPosts component).
Special behaviors: Maintains audit trail; supports escalation workflow and status updates.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each content report entry.
- `reported_post_id`: Target post's [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts) reported for violation or moderation. May also be used to reference a comment if required.
- `reporter_member_id`: Reporting member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members), if the reporter is a registered member.
- `reporter_guest_id`: Reporting guest's [discussionboard_guests.id](#discussionboard_guests), if the report was filed by a guest user (optional).
- `report_reason`: Reason for content report - Implements requirement to capture user's motivation for reporting content. Ensures normalization by storing only reason text; examples include 'spam', 'abuse', 'off-topic', etc. Required for moderation triage and analytics.
- `status`: Moderation status of the report - Implements status tracking for the moderation queue. Allowed values are 'pending', 'in_review', 'action_taken', 'dismissed', reflecting different workflow states. Ensures normalization by storing only the status token. For example, 'pending' is assigned on creation.
- `reported_at`: Timestamp when the content was reported - Implements audit trail requirement and ensures detailed moderation history. Not nullable.
- `moderator_note`: Moderator's note on review outcome - Allows documenting justification for resolution or further actions. Nullable; present after moderator review.

### `discussionboard_moderation_actions`

Moderation Action Entity - Implements requirement for logging all actions taken by moderators or admins in response to reports, violations, or escalations as described in 'Features and Functional Specifications' and 'Business Rules and Policies'.

This model records every action taken during moderation (warning issued, thread locked, post deleted, user suspended, etc.), who performed it, and on which content or user. Maintains 3NF by linking actions to actors (moderator/admin), target content or users, and report IDs if applicable. E.g., When a moderator deletes a post for policy violation, this logs the event with details.

Key relationships: Relates to moderation actor, affected user (optional), and reported content. Also links to the report if action was a result of a report.
Special behaviors: Immutable audit log for compliance and appeals.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each moderation action.
- `moderator_id`: Actor's [discussionboard_moderators.id](#discussionboard_moderators) who performed the action. Required for accountability.
- `report_id`: Related report's [discussionboard_content_reports.id](#discussionboard_content_reports), if this action is linked to a content report. Nullable, as some actions may be proactive.
- `affected_post_id`: Target content's [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts) affected by this action. Nullable, as some actions are user-account-related, not specific content.
- `affected_member_id`: Affected member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members), if the action concerns a user account. For example, suspensions or warnings.
- `action_type`: Type of moderation action taken - Implements audit trail and compliance requirements. Examples: 'warned', 'deleted_post', 'suspended_user', 'locked_thread', 'archived_thread'. Only atomic state; details are in the description. Keeps the table normalized. For example, 'warned' or 'deleted_post'.
- `action_description`: Detailed description for the action - Implements need for justification and appeals. Ensures normalization by keeping only description in text. E.g., 'Post contained prohibited content per rule X.'
- `action_timestamp`: Timestamp of the moderation action - Implements audit trail and sequencing of moderation events.

### `discussionboard_warning_logs`

Warning Log Entity - Implements the requirement for tracking all warnings issued to members, as per acceptance criteria in User Roles, Functional Specifications, and Business Rules.

Each warning issued by a moderator/admin to a member is logged here, maintaining normalized structure by linking to both the issuer and recipient, along with reason and timestamp. For example, when a moderator warns a member for minor misconduct, this captures the event.

Key relationships: Links warning to the moderator (actor) and warned member (recipient), referencing both by IDs.
Special behaviors: Used for history checks and appeals, supports escalation of repeated violations.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each warning log.
- `moderator_id`: Moderator/admin's [discussionboard_moderators.id](#discussionboard_moderators) who issued the warning. Required for accountability.
- `warned_member_id`: Member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members) who received the warning.
- `warning_reason`: Reason for the warning - Implements requirement for capturing justification. Maintains normalization (atomic text value). E.g., 'inappropriate language' or 'off-topic reply'.
- `issued_at`: Timestamp when the warning was issued. Ensures auditability and time-order analysis. Not nullable.

### `discussionboard_suspensions`

Suspension Log Entity - Implements the requirement for tracking temporary user suspensions for policy violations or moderation reasons. Referenced in User Roles & Authentication, Functional Specifications, and Business Rules.

This model logs suspension actions with start/end timestamps, reason, actor (moderator/admin), and target member. Fully normalized; does not pre-calculate any suspension history summary. For example, if a member is suspended for spamming, a row is created here with dates and cause.

Key relationships: Links moderator (actor) and suspended member (recipient).
Special behaviors: Supports enforcement of suspensions and review for appeals or admin audit.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each user suspension record.
- `moderator_id`: Moderator/admin's [discussionboard_moderators.id](#discussionboard_moderators) who performed the suspension.
- `suspended_member_id`: Member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members) who was suspended.
- `suspension_reason`: Reason suspension was issued - Implements requirement for tracking policy violations or abuse. Maintains 3NF (atomic value only). E.g., 'spamming', 'multiple policy violations'.
- `suspension_started_at`: When suspension began - For audit trails and auto-expiry systems. Maintains precise timeline for enforcement.
- `suspension_ends_at`: Scheduled end time for suspension - For auto-lifting suspensions and appeals. Null if indefinite or until manual review.

### `discussionboard_bans`

Ban Log Entity - Implements requirement for permanent user bans, as mandated in User Roles, Policies, and Auditing documentation.

Each row represents a permanent ban issued to a member (or, rare, a guest) by an admin; records cause, actor, issue time, and optional notes. Maintains normalized structure: each ban is atomic and links to relevant actor and user entities. For example, if an admin bans a member for repeated malicious activity, a record is created here.

Key relationships: Connects banned user (usually a member) and banning admin. May also target guests in some edge cases.
Special behaviors: Used for enforcement, audit, and appeals; notifies affected users per requirements.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each ban record.
- `banned_member_id`: Member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members) who has been permanently banned.
- `banned_guest_id`: Guest's [discussionboard_guests.id](#discussionboard_guests) who has been permanently banned (rare; usually members).
- `admin_id`: Admin's [discussionboard_admins.id](#discussionboard_admins) who performed the ban.
- `ban_reason`: Reason for the permanent ban - Implements tracking and appeal justification. Maintains 3NF (atomic value). E.g., 'repeated malicious activity' or 'severe policy breach'.
- `banned_at`: Ban issue timestamp - For system notification and legal reference. Not nullable.
- `notes`: Optional admin notes for the ban - Used for details and audit trail. Nullable and not required for all bans.

### `discussionboard_post_reactions`

Post reaction entity - Implements the 'User Interactions and Engagement' requirement from the specifications. Each record is a normalized log of a user's emoji or symbolic response to a post. Maintains 3NF by having a single atomic value per reaction, with unique constraints over (post, member, type). For example, a member may react with a 'heart' emoji to a post.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Serves as the unique identifier for the model instance.
- `discussionboard_post_id`: Target post's [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts). The post that received the reaction. Normalized foreign key.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Reacting member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). The user who gave the reaction. Normalized foreign key.
- `reaction_type`: Type of reaction (e.g., emoji name or standard). Atomic value, e.g., 'thumbs_up', 'heart'.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of when the reaction was created for audit and time queries.

### `discussionboard_post_likes`

Post like entity - Implements binary 'like' from a member to a post. Maintains 3NF by storing only atomic likes (one like per user per post). For example, if a member likes a post, that action appears only once in the table. Unique over (post, member).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Serves as the unique identifier for the model instance.
- `discussionboard_post_id`: Liked post's [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts). References the liked post in a normalized manner.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Liking member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). The member who liked the post. Normalized foreign key.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the like was recorded.

### `discussionboard_polls`

Poll metadata entity - Implements member-driven polls inside threads. Represents an atomic poll question, its configuration, and creator. Maintains 3NF by not storing any derived results. Each poll is linked to a parent thread and a creator. Example: a poll about preferred economic policy within a thread.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Serves as the unique identifier for the model instance.
- `discussionboard_thread_id`: Thread's [discussionboard_threads.id](#discussionboard_threads). References the discussion thread this poll is attached to.
- `created_by_member_id`: Creator member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). Member who started the poll, as normalized foreign key.
- `prompt`: Poll prompt shown to users. For example: 'Which policy is best?'
- `allow_multiple_choices`: Allow voters to choose more than one option. True for multi-select polls.
- `is_anonymous`: Indicates if the poll is anonymous. True means individual votes are hidden.
- `expires_at`: Poll expiration timestamp. Nullable if the poll never expires.
- `created_at`: When the poll was created.

### `discussionboard_poll_votes`

Poll voting entity - Each record shows a member's atomic vote for a poll option. Enforces strict 3NF with unique over (poll, member, option) for multi-choice, or per poll in single-choice situation. Used for direct normalization of poll voting results. Example: If a user votes Option A on Poll 1, that's one row.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Serves as the unique identifier for the model instance.
- `discussionboard_poll_id`: Owns to poll [discussionboard_polls.id](#discussionboard_polls). The poll this vote is for.
- `voting_member_id`: Member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). The voter who cast this ballot.
- `selected_option`: User-selected value (poll option label or id if normalized elsewhere).
- `created_at`: When this vote was cast.

### `discussionboard_mentions`

Mention (tagging) entity for posts/comments. Captures normalized reference to a mention of a member within a post. Maintains 3NF—each mention is a single entry relating post and mentioned member, supporting notification infrastructure. Unique for (post, mentioned member) pairs.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Serves as the unique identifier for the model instance.
- `discussionboard_post_id`: Post's [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts). Points to the location where the mention occurred.
- `mentioned_member_id`: Mentioned user's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). The user referenced in the post/comment.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this mention was created, used for notification ordering.

### `discussionboard_notifications`

Discussion Board Notification - This implements the notification delivery and alerting requirement from the requirements documents (particularly 03_discussionboard_features_and_functional_specifications.md, section 7 Notifications and Alerts; see also user journeys and business rules). 

Business explanation: Stores detailed notifications generated by the system—such as mentions, replies, moderator actions, and administrative announcements—to be delivered to specific users. Ensures users are promptly informed of activity requiring their attention. Maintains full 3NF compliance: notification text, type, and linkage to recipient are atomic and non-redundant. For example, when a user is mentioned in a comment, a notification is created here detailing the context and recipient. 

Key relationships: References discussionboard_members as notification recipient; may also reference other entities (e.g., post/thread) as optional context if needed (not included here, but ID pattern allows for future extension). 
Special behaviors: Soft deletion via nullable deleted_at; status/opened flag; delivery details and related timestamps for auditability and analytics; all notifications are individualized and immutable after creation. Audit trails of delivery status handled within this model.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each notification record. Ensures entity uniqueness and supports distributed environments. Required for all entities for tracking and referencing.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Recipient's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). Indicates which member this notification is intended for. Enables delivery targeting and audit trail. Required for all notifications.
- `type`: Notification type - Implements requirement for distinguishing system, user, moderation, and announcement notifications. Possible values: 'mention', 'reply', 'moderator_action', 'announcement', etc. Ensures clear categorization for UI badge and analytics. Example: When a thread is locked, moderators receive a 'moderator_action' type notification. Atomic and fully normalized.
- `title`: Notification title or brief summary - Implements clear communication of subject as required by UX guidelines. Summarizes notification content in a single line for user display. Example: 'You were mentioned in a post.' Fully normalized.
- `body`: Full textual content of the notification - Implements rich, readable notification context as required by the user journey and business rules. Contains detailed context such as source thread or action taken. Example: 'Your post in "2025 Elections Economy" was edited by a moderator.'
- `url`: Optional URI to direct recipient to the notification context. Supports quick navigation to relevant thread, post, or profile. Implements UX quick-access requirement. Example: '/thread/abc123/post/xyz456'.
- `opened`: Whether the notification has been opened/read by the recipient - Implements user status tracking for badge counts & UX feedback. Example: New notifications are false; becomes true when user visits notification center or clicks link. Fully normalized with no redundant status.
- `created_at`: Notification creation timestamp. Implements requirement to log when notifications are generated, for both UX ordering and audit trails. Non-nullable for history and analytics purposes.
- `opened_at`: Timestamp when the notification was opened/read. Enables precise auditing and user interaction analytics. Nullable for unopened notifications. Ensures atomic status-tracking in 3NF structure.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp. Implements compliance with audit and retention policies. Marks notification as deleted (hidden from end-user), but retention for admin/audit. Nullable; only set on soft delete.

### `discussionboard_alerts`

Discussion Board Alert - Implements the alerts/urgent notifications requirement from the requirements analysis (03_discussionboard_features_and_functional_specifications.md, section 7; plus cross-reference with moderation & audit policies). 

Business explanation: This table stores urgent, high-visibility system or policy alerts targeted at users, typically for critical events (e.g., suspension warnings, urgent moderation outcomes, system-wide updates). Alerts are designed to demand prominent attention in user UI compared to routine notifications. Fully 3NF: each alert is atomic, unrelated fields and entity-specific details are externalized, audit events logged separately. For example, if a member is suspended, an alert is generated and displayed in a prominent banner.

Key relationships: References discussionboard_members for alert recipient.
Special behaviors: Alerts are prioritized for UI, include severity/type, full body, status, and are audited with timestamps. Could link to moderation/incident report context (future extension).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for this alert, ensuring system-wide traceability and immutability.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Recipient's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). Indicates which member this alert is for. Delivers alerts to the user's alert center or dashboard. Mandatory foreign key reference.
- `type`: Alert type/category - Implements requirement to indicate nature and urgency (e.g., 'suspension_warning', 'policy_update', 'system_notice', 'important_announcement'). Used in UI sorting/filtering and analytics. Atomic and normalized.
- `severity`: Severity level of the alert (e.g., 'critical', 'warning', 'info'). Implements requirement to differentiate UI treatment. Example: 'critical' triggers red banner; 'info' is less intrusive. Fully normalized, non-redundant.
- `title`: Short alert headline - Implements prominent display and user clarity on subject. Example: 'Suspension Warning'. Used for attention-grabbing summaries in alerts center. Normalized for search/display.
- `body`: Full body of the alert - Implements detailed communication requirement for urgent incidents. Contains full explanation, relevant context, and actionable guidance. Example: 'Your account is suspended for policy violation XYZ.' Atomic, normalized.
- `is_active`: Alert is currently active and should be shown to user. Implements business rule for auto-dismissing resolved alerts, supports front-end badge logic, and analytics. Example: Suspension alert is_active until reinstated. Non-redundant, atomic trimmed down to status.
- `created_at`: When the alert was generated. Supports audit and time-sequencing in UI. Fully normalized, required for analytics. Non-nullable.
- `resolved_at`: When the alert was marked as resolved/dismissed by system or recipient. Implements ability to archive past high-severity alerts, supports analytics on resolution speed. Nullable for active/unresolved alerts only. 3NF compliant.

### `discussionboard_search_histories`

User-initiated search activity log - This implements the history and analytics requirements from the requirements analysis (Features and Functional Specifications: Section 5 - Search, Filtering, and Discovery). Records each search operation performed by a user, tied to their account if available or anonymized if performed by a guest, along with search keywords, filter usage, and timestamp. Maintains 3NF by storing only atomic search operation data. For example, a member searching for 'budget deficit' will trigger an entry recording their member ID, search query, selected filters, and time of search. Key relationships: Optionally references member actor from already existing actors table discussionboard_members via foreign key. Special behaviors: Soft-deletion possible, sensitive to privacy controls; no computed result counts included.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Globally unique identifier for each search history record.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Related member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members) if search is performed by authenticated member. Null if guest or unauthenticated.
- `search_query`: Search text entered by user - Implements the requirement for recording used keywords. Stores the exact query string submitted.
- `used_filters`: Serialized list of filter identifiers applied during search. Implements analytics and recall requirements. For example: 'tag:macroeconomics,section:current_events'.
- `executed_at`: Timestamp when the search was performed. Implements chronology and audit trail requirements.
- `deleted_at`: Soft-deletion timestamp, null if active. Supports log cleanup, rights to be forgotten, and privacy controls.

### `discussionboard_tagged_threads`

Thread-tag link (junction table) - Implements associating threads with tags for flexible discovery and search. This is a junction table supporting a M:N relationship between discussionboard_threads and discussionboard_thread_tags. Fully normalized, containing only atomic foreign keys and the created_at timestamp. For instance, if a thread is tagged with 'fiscal policy' and 'budget', there will be two entries (one per tag) in this table. Key relationships: Links a thread from discussionboard_threads and a tag from discussionboard_thread_tags. Special behaviors: Enforces uniqueness on (thread, tag) pair, supports fast lookup for search and filtering, includes creation timestamp for audit trail.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each thread-tag relationship instance.
- `discussionboard_thread_id`: Targeted thread's [discussionboard_threads.id](#discussionboard_threads). Enables linking to a thread entity.
- `discussionboard_thread_tag_id`: Associated tag's [discussionboard_thread_tags.id](#discussionboard_thread_tags). Enables M:N association.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of tag assignment. Implements auditability and order-by-recent requirement.

### `discussionboard_thread_tags`

Discussion thread tag library - Implements tagging, search, and organization requirements, allowing tag-based topic discovery and moderation. This table stores a catalog of available tags that can be assigned to threads, such as 'economy', 'election', or 'policy'. Maintains 3NF by not including aggregate info, only atomic tag data. For example, site admin creates/tag 'fiscal_policy', which members can assign to threads. Key relationships: Referenced by tagged-thread junction table. Uniqueness by code. Special behaviors: Tag codes are unique, names are searchable, can be marked as moderated/restricted via flags.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique ID for each tag definition.
- `code`: Canonical tag code. Implements uniqueness and fast search requirement. Lower-case alphanumeric/underscore.
- `display_name`: Tag display name, e.g. 'Fiscal Policy'. User-friendly labeling.
- `description`: Explanation or usage guideline for this tag. Fulfills moderation/discussion guideline mapping. Nullable if not present.
- `is_restricted`: Tag moderation flag. If true, only moderators/admins can assign tag. Implements requirements for moderated tags.
- `is_hidden`: Soft deprecation flag. If true, users should not see/assign this tag except admin.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of tag creation. Implements audit trail.
- `updated_at`: Last updated. Allows admin track of edits to tags.

### `discussionboard_filters`

Saved search/filter configuration - Implements the 'filters' and 'recall/discovery tools', for example, members saving useful filter sets for fast access or sharing. Records configurations for reusable search or discovery filters, which can be user-specific (member) or system-wide. Strictly 3NF: only atomic filter info. For example, a member can save a filter called 'Recent Elections' for all threads with tag 'elections' in 'current events' section, stored as a JSON or string formula. Key relationships: References member for user-specific filters via foreign key. System-wide filters are marked by null member id. Special behaviors: Unique name per user, supports public/private visibility, allows deletion (soft).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. ID for each filter definition.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Filter owner's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members) if user-specific. Null if shared/system-wide.
- `name`: Name for this filter as seen by user. Unique per owner (enforced by index). Atomic string. For example: 'Recent Macroeconomics'.
- `definition`: Serialized filter definition (could be a query language or JSON-based formula). For example: '{tags: ["elections"], section: "current_events"}'.
- `is_public`: Visibility setting. True if filter is shared or system-wide, false if private to member.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of filter creation. For filtering, order-by, and audit.
- `updated_at`: Last updated. For management and recall tools.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion (null if active). For removal and right-to-be-forgotten policies.

### `discussionboard_business_rules`

Business Rule Definition - This implements the requirement for system-wide governance and operational rules, mapped from section 5.1 of the requirements analysis (Business Rules and Policies). 

Defines a single rule with versioning and enforcement notes, allowing traceability of policy enforcement. Maintains 3NF by storing only atomic rule data, with version history tracked elsewhere. For example, 'No hate speech' or 'Maximum post length'.

Key relationships: May be referenced by platform policy and audit log entities. 
Special behaviors: Immutable after approval except via re-versioning.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each business rule record.
- `rule_code`: Machine-friendly rule code - Implements unique policy identification as a short string (e.g., 'NO_HATE_SPEECH'). Facilitates referencing and linking, enforcing uniqueness per rule.
- `title`: Rule short title - The human-readable name for the rule, for display and audit references. Ensures normalization by storing only the atomic rule label. Used in rule listings and selection forms.
- `description`: Rule full description - The verbose requirements, restrictions, and definitions for this rule. Maintains normalization by excluding enforcement history or modification logs; only static rule details. Used for admin summaries and user display.
- `is_active`: Rule activation flag - Determines if this business rule is currently in effect. Implements EARS specifications for system behavioral toggling; referenced when evaluating enforcement eligibility.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of rule entry creation. Used for audit and historical reference; never updated.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last rule information update (not enforcement event). Tracked only for rule text changes, not enforcement or violation logging.

### `discussionboard_platform_policies`

Platform Policy Statement - Implements explicit documentation and versioning of the platform's rules and policies, based on requirements in the Business Rules and Policies document (section 1 and 3).

Captures high-level policy texts and their publication states, ensuring compliance with audit and transparency values. Maintains 3NF by not embedding related actions, incidents, or appeals.

Usage example: Published privacy policy, content moderation policy, or terms of service, referenced in user interfaces and admin dashboards.

Key relationships: May be linked in notifications or user onboarding flows.
Special behaviors: Replaces previous versions on update; policy text is immutable once published.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each platform policy document.
- `policy_code`: Unique policy code - Implements compliance requirement for distinct identification (e.g., 'PRIVACY', 'MODERATION'). Used for referencing and policy change tracking. Enforces uniqueness per active policy.
- `title`: Policy title - Human-readable title for display and search. Maintains normalization by excluding policy text or status.
- `policy_text`: Policy content - The full published text of the policy, supporting platform communication transparency and legal reference. For user agreement and admin review screens.
- `is_active`: Policy activation flag - Indicates if this version of the policy is currently in force. Supports rollback on major rule changes.
- `published_at`: Publication timestamp - The datetime this policy was rendered active. Used in compliance audits; immutable after creation.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp for this policy entry. Tracks administrative changes only, not user or enforcement logs. Required for policy update audit trails.

### `discussionboard_audit_logs`

System Audit Log Entry - Implements the audit trail requirements for sensitive operations, as described in the Security Requirements and Data Retention sections.

Captures each critical action for traceability, legal compliance, and operational review. Maintains 3NF by linking only to atomic action data with foreign keys for originators if implemented in other schemas.

Usage: Whenever a mod/admin changes a rule, enforces a suspension, or alters system access. Allows search by actor, action type, or time window.

Key relationships: May point to actors by actor_id if available.
Special behaviors: Entries are strictly append-only; never updated or deleted except by court order.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each audit log entry.
- `action_type`: Action type code - Implements requirement for specific action tracking (e.g., 'RULE_EDIT', 'SUSPENSION_APPLY'). Supports compliance reporting without embedding further context.
- `description`: Detailed description of the action event taken, for compliance traceability. Maintains normalization by storing only the fact of the action, not duplicating target entity data.
- `actor_id`: UUID of the actor (admin/moderator/member) who performed the action. May reference discussionboard_admins, discussionboard_moderators, or discussionboard_members in Actors schema for referential consistency. Nullable to allow system actions.
- `target_id`: UUID of the primary entity affected (user, post, policy, etc.). Usage depends on action type. May reference models in other schemas or be null for system-wide actions.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of audit log creation. Recorded at the moment of action; immutable.

### `discussionboard_incident_reports`

Incident Report Entity - Implements the incident reporting and escalation workflows from Business Rules and Policies section 4.

Logs reports of rule/policy violations, capturing status, reporting party, action taken (if any), and timestamps. Maintains strict normalization by avoiding embedding of user or policy details; only links by code or ID where necessary. 
Usage example: A member or moderator submits a report of a suspected violation. Tracked through review, escalation, closure.

Key relationships: actor_id and possibly related audit_logs or policies.
Special behaviors: Once closed, cannot be edited; only reopened with admin approval for audits.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Report Identifier.
- `incident_code`: Incident code - Unique identifier for each incident (e.g., 'INCIDENT-20240321-001'). Allows search, link to audit logs, and escalation procedures.
- `status`: Incident status - Workflow indicator (e.g., 'OPEN', 'IN_REVIEW', 'CLOSED', 'ESCALATED'). Implements incident state requirement; supports escalation triggers and closure rules. (Enum recommended in app logic).
- `reporter_id`: Actor who submitted the report. UUID value; may reference admins, moderators, or members in Actors schema. Nullable if submitted anonymously.
- `description`: Incident details - Free text provided by the reporter explaining facts and relevant context. Maintains normalization by not including structured rule data; only the reported statement.
- `created_at`: Incident report creation timestamp - Used to measure response SLA and escalation timing.
- `updated_at`: Last incident status update (e.g., progress, assignment, closure). Used for internal audit and dashboard tracking.

### `discussionboard_appeals`

Appeal Record - Implements the appeals process for disciplinary or moderation outcomes, as required by the Business Rules and Policies (section 5), including role-based appeal rights and audit trails.

Captures every user-submitted appeal with status and outcome details. Maintains 3NF by recording only atomic data and referencing related incidents or users by ID or code, not duplicating content.

Usage: A sanctioned user (e.g., after a suspension or ban recorded elsewhere) appeals a decision; each appeal is logged with outcome and timestamps.

Key relationships: reporter_id, possibly related incident report or moderation action (cross-schema). 
Special behaviors: Once closed, appeals are immutable; status may affect complaint metrics.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique appeal record identifier.
- `appeal_code`: Unique appeal code (e.g., 'APPEAL-20240321-205'). Ensures tracking and cross-referencing with incidents and audit logs.
- `status`: Appeal status workflow value (e.g., 'PENDING', 'REVIEWING', 'UPHELD', 'REJECTED'). Enables SLA and dashboard reporting; suggested as an Enum in app logic. Maintains normalization by not storing duplicate status details.
- `appellant_id`: UUID of user who filed the appeal (may be admin, moderator, or member). Nullable for anonymous, though unusual. Cross-references the Actors models for full details.
- `incident_id`: If linked to an incident report, holds the corresponding report's ID for audit and workflow consistency. Nullable for general appeals not tied to a specific incident.
- `outcome`: Outcome memo - Short description of the appeal's result once closed (e.g., 'Ban upheld', 'Suspension reversed'). Maintains normalization by storing only atomic outcome description, not related evidence or reasoning.
- `created_at`: Appeal submission timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last appeal update timestamp (e.g., outcome decided, status changed).

operations.description: This endpoint retrieves a paginated, searchable, and sortable list of discussion board configurations. It is intended for administrative purposes. The operation supports filtering based on fields of the discussionboard_configurations table: id (UUID primary key for each configuration), name (unique configuration key, e.g., 'default_section_policy'), settings_json (board/section behavioral settings as a JSON string), and description (human-readable explanation). There are no soft or hard delete fields in this schema; all records are persistent and updates are handled via PUT. This endpoint does not support creation or modification—only complex queries for existing configurations for audit or configuration management. Related endpoint for individual retrieval: GET /discussionboardConfigurations/{configurationId}.

description.description: 카테고리 설명, UI/관리자 안내 등에서 사용. 형식은 문자열 또는 null(미기재시).

order.description:
카테고리 표시 순서 (오름차순으로 UI에 배치됨).
동일 섹션 내에서만 의미 있음.

enabled.description: 카테고리 사용 가능 여부. 활성화(true) 시 노출/작성 가능, 비활성(false)이면 숨김/쓰기 불가.

IDiscussionboardCategory.description:
토론 게시판의 카테고리 단위 엔티티 스키마.

Prisma discussionboard_categories 테이블 전체 컬럼을 망라하며,
비즈니스 설명 및 각 컬럼 주석을 포함합니다.
다른 엔티티(예: thread, section)와의 관계 및 리스트 구성에 참고.

discussionboard_section_id.description: 카테고리가 소속될 섹션의 id(FK). Prisma discussionboard_categories.discussionboard_section_id 에 해당합니다.

oneOf.description: 카테고리 설명 (nullable, 미입력시 null)
카테고리 설명 (nullable, 미입력시 null)

description.description: 카테고리 설명 (nullable, 미입력시 null)

IDiscussionboardCategory.ICreate.description:
카테고리 등록 시 사용되는 요청 바디 타입입니다.

Prisma discussionboard_categories 스키마의 생성 컬럼을 모두 포함하며, id 필드는 생성 시 자동 할당되므로 제외됩니다.

Security: creator_id 등 작성자 사용자 id를 직접 받지 않으며, 인증 컨텍스트에서 획득하여 사용합니다.

discussionboard_section_id.description:
수정 대상 카테고리가 소속될 섹션 (nullable 아님).
변경 가능한 FK입니다.

name.description: 카테고리의 새 이름입니다. 비어있지 않은 문자열이어야 하며, 해당 섹션 내에서 유니크 조건을 만족해야 합니다.

oneOf.description: 카테고리 설명, null 가능
카테고리 설명, null 가능

description.description: 카테고리 설명, null 가능

order.description: 표시 순서 정수값, UI 개편 시 변경될 수 있습니다.

enabled.description: 활성/비활성화 여부. false로 할 경우 UI/작성/노출 차단

IDiscussionboardCategory.IUpdate.description:
카테고리 정보 수정 요청 타입.

Prisma discussionboard_categories 테이블의 컬럼 중 실제 수정 가능한 요소 집합만 포함합니다.
id는 URL 파라미터로 별도 지정되고, 나머지가 request body 값에 포함됩니다.

id.description:
관리자 역할 PK
관리자 배정/조회용 FK로 활용 또는 직접 관리 ID 사용

IDiscussionboardAdmin.IRequest.description: 관리자 역할 레코드 검색/필터/정렬용 요청 오브젝트입니다.

data.description: 관리자 역할 배정 레코드 배열

IPageIDiscussionboardAdmin.description: 관리자 역할 엔티티(assignment) 목록을 페이징 결과로 담는 표준 컨테이너 타입.

id.description:
관리자 역할 고유 식별자 (주민)

Prisma discussionboard_admins.id 컬럼

created_at.description:
관리자 역할 부여 시각 (ISO8601).
Prisma discussionboard_admins.created_at 컬럼, 권한 부여 히스토리 관리 목적 등.

IDiscussionboardAdmin.description:
관리자 역할 배정 엔티티 타입입니다.

Prisma의 discussionboard_admins 테이블 전체 컬럼 대비, id, created_at 필드만 정의되어 있습니다. 관리자 권한의 부여 및 감사/조회의 엔티티 단위로 사용합니다.

id.description:
관리자 역할 배정(부여)할 대상 계정의 고유 id (FK)
외부 user/member 엔티티와 1:1 매핑하는 uuid 값.

created_at.description: 관리자 역할 배정 시각. 자동 입력이 권장되지만, 관리도구에서 값 변경이 필요시 수동 입력 지원.

IDiscussionboardAdmin.ICreate.description:
관리자 역할 할당 요청 바디 타입.
이에 직접적으로 password, creator_id 등 민감정보가 포함되지 않으며 인증과정에서만 외부 인증이 요구됨. Prisma schema 구조에 맞춰 요청 값을 제공합니다.

created_at.description: 관리자 역할 배정시각(업데이트 시점에 재할당 가능)

IDiscussionboardAdmin.IUpdate.description:
본인 관리자 역할 엔트리 업데이트 요청 타입.

업데이트 허용 필드는 created_at에 한정하며, id는 path에 명시/불변입니다.

id.description: 모더레이터 역할 PK

IDiscussionboardModerator.IRequest.description: 게시판 모더레이터 역할 배정/검색 등에서 사용되는 검색 파라미터 오브젝트

IPageIDiscussionboardModerator.description: discussionboard_moderators 목록을 페이징 결과로 리턴하는 컨테이너입니다.

id.description:
고유한 모더레이터 역할 식별자입니다. discussionboard_moderators 테이블의 주 키로, 시스템 내 역할 할당을 명확히 추적합니다.

각 모더레이터 배정 문서에 사용되며, 다른 도메인(멤버/유저)과 외래키로 연관될 수 있습니다.

created_at.description:
모더레이터 역할이 부여된 시점을 나타내는 타임스탬프입니다.

감사 추적, 커뮤니티 신뢰도 분석, 역할 변동 이력 확인에 반드시 필요합니다.

IDiscussionboardModerator.description:
정치·경제 토론 게시판에서 커뮤니티 관리를 담당하는 모더레이터 역할 배정 정보를 정의합니다.

requirements analysis 문서와 Prisma discussionboard_moderators 모델(Actors) 설명에 근거하여, 각 배정 건의 식별자와 역할 시작 시점만 엄격히 기록합니다. 모든 속성은 정규화 규칙과 개인정보 보호 원칙을 중점적으로 반영합니다.

id.description: 부여할 모더레이터 역할의 고유 식별자입니다. 멤버/유저의 ID와 매핑되는 UUID이며, 외부 참조에서 유효성이 보장되어야 합니다.

created_at.description: 모더레이터 권한이 할당된 실제 일시로, 시스템 레벨에서 기록/자동 부여합니다.

IDiscussionboardModerator.ICreate.description:
모더레이터 역할 신규 배정 시 사용하는 요청 데이터 타입입니다.

discussionboard_moderators 테이블의 구조를 그대로 따라, 해당 역할 할당의 유일 식별자와 부여 일시만 포함합니다. 추가 개인정보나 계정정보, 'deleted_at', 'assigned_by' 등은 절대 포함하지 않습니다.

id.description: 수정 대상 모더레이터 배정 레코드의 고유 식별자입니다.

created_at.description: 모더레이터 권한 배정 일시로, 필요한 경우 갱신될 수 있습니다.

IDiscussionboardModerator.IUpdate.description:
기존 모더레이터 역할 배정 정보를 수정할 때 사용하는 타입입니다.

수정 가능한 속성은 schema 상 명시된 필드뿐이며, 특히 사적으로 처리되어야 하는 추가 메타데이터, 삭제 플래그, 감사 로그 등은 포함하지 않습니다.

id.description: (옵션) 멤버 식별자(회원 역할 할당 UUID) 기준으로 필터링할 때 사용합니다.

created_at.description: (옵션) 회원 역할이 부여된 시점(타임스탬프)으로 검색 조건에 활용할 수 있습니다.

page.description: 페이징 시 요청 페이지 번호 (1부터 시작).

limit.description: 한 페이지 내 결과 수. 기본값은 시스템 정책(예: 100)을 따릅니다.

IDiscussionboardMembers.IRequest.description:
discussionboard_members 엔터티(회원 역할 등록)에 대한 list/search/pagination 요구를 처리하기 위한 필터, 검색, 페이징 요청 타입입니다.

특정 id나 생성일자 기준 정렬, 부분 검색, 페이지네이션 모두 지원하며, Prisma 스키마 규칙만을 따릅니다.

data.description: 결과 회원 목록 (각 엔트리의 필드는 스키마 제한과 개인정보 원칙을 철저히 따름)

IPageIDiscussionboardMembers.description:
회원 역할 배정(entity: discussionboard_members) 결과 페이징 컨테이너 타입입니다.

표준 IPage<T> 구조에 따라 목록, 페이지 정보, total count 등 반환합니다.

id.description: 회원 역할을 위한 고유 식별자 (UUID). 회원계정/유저 관리 도메인과의 참조를 통한 유일성 확보 목적입니다.

created_at.description: 회원 역할(멤버십)이 처음 생성/등록된 시점. 가입, 승격 등의 시나리오에서 사용됩니다. 정책 및 감사 추적 등 다양한 비즈니스 요건을 충족합니다.

IDiscussionboardMembers.description:
정치·경제 토론 게시판에서 시스템 회원 역할을 부여 받은 모든 엔트리(가입자, 인증 유저)의 원자적 배정정보 구조입니다.

Prisma discussionboard_members 모델과 requirements analysis의 보안·권한체계 명세를 근거로 하며, 프로필·이메일·패스워드·탈퇴 등 민감한 속성은 전혀 포함하지 않습니다.

id.description: 신규 회원 역할 할당을 위한 고유 식별자(UUID)입니다. 회원계정 생성 흐름과 분리되어 관리되며, 외부 참조와 결합될 수 있습니다.

created_at.description: 회원 역할 생성 시점(ISO 8601); 일반적으로 시스템이 자동 지정합니다.

IDiscussionboardMembers.ICreate.description:
회원 역할 신규 등록 시 사용하는 요청 타입입니다.

필수 필드는 id(UUID)와 created_at(등록일) 뿐이고, 추가 인증이나 개인정보 관련 속성은 정책상 별도 관리됨을 주의하세요.

id.description: 수정 대상 회원 역할의 고유 식별자입니다. PK로 immutable이므로 실제로는 거의 사용되지 않으며, Prisma 스키마와 완전일치합니다.

created_at.description: 회원 역할 배정 일시로, 실제 갱신 가능성은 제한적이나 구조적으로 포함하며, 정책상 이력 회귀가 필요한 경우 사용합니다.

IDiscussionboardMembers.IUpdate.description:
회원 역할 등록 정보 수정 시 사용할 요청 타입입니다.

수정 가능한 속성은 스키마 상의 필드(id, created_at)만 포함하고, 추가 개인정보, 이메일, 회원 탈퇴 등은 해당 도메인의 별도 API에서 관리합니다.

id.description: (옵션) 게스트 식별자 기준으로 검색 시 사용

created_at.description:
(옵션) 게스트 역할이 생성된 타임스탬프

의미 있는 기간 또는 세션 분류별로 필터링

limit.description: 페이지당 결과 기록 수(기본값 시스템 정책 적용)

IDiscussionboardGuests.IRequest.description:
게스트(비회원 역할) 역할 엔터티에 대한 리스트/페이징/검색 요청 타입입니다.

discussionboard_guests 테이블(Actors) 구조를 근거로, id, create_at, 페이지네이션 옵션만 지원합니다.

data.description: 게스트 역할 할당 목록

IPageIDiscussionboardGuests.description:
게스트 역할 배정(비회원) 목록 결과에 대한 표준 IPage<T> 타입 컨테이너입니다.

data 필드에는 한 페이지만큼의 guest entity들이 반환되며, 모두 개인정보 최소화 정책 및 스키마 정의만 따릅니다.

id.description: 비회원/게스트 역할을 추적하기 위한 unique 식별자(UUID)입니다. guest 세션이나 방문자를 익명 식별자로 관리할 때 사용합니다.

created_at.description: 게스트 역할(또는 세션, 방문 기록) 등록 시각. 기간별 분석, 개선, 전환율 추적 등 다양한 용도로 활용 가능합니다.

IDiscussionboardGuests.description:
정치·경제 토론 게시판에서 익명 방문자나 비회원의 역할 할당(guest role tracking)에 사용되는 entity 타입입니다.

discussionboard_guests Prisma 모델 규정과 개인정보 최소화 원칙을 철저하게 준수하며, 유저 식별 외에는 어떤 세부 정보도 반환하지 않습니다.

id.description: 새 게스트(비회원) 역할 할당을 위한 식별자(UUID). 방문 세션 관리나 익명 추적을 위함

created_at.description: 할당 일시(ISO 8601); 게스트 역할 시작시 서버가 자동 부여

IDiscussionboardGuests.ICreate.description:
새 방문자(게스트) 역할 할당 시 사용하는 생성 요청 타입입니다.

필수 값은 id와 created_at이며, 기타 인증·개인식별 정보는 별도 테이블/서비스에서 관리합니다.

id.description:
고유 게스트 식별자, 예: UUID. 'discussionboard_guests' 테이블의 PK와 매핑됩니다.

이 값은 보통 방문자 세션이나 익명 토큰을 식별하는 데 사용됩니다.

created_at.description:
게스트 신규 배정/세션 생성 시각. 'discussionboard_guests' 테이블의 'created_at'과 1:1 매핑됩니다.

게스트가 사이트를 탐색하기 시작한 시간을 기록하며, 효과적인 관리와 추세 분석·정책 적용 시점 기준값입니다.

IDiscussionboardGuests.IUpdate.description:
게스트 역할 배정 엔터티(discussionboard_guests 테이블) 갱신용에 해당합니다.

UUID PK(id)와 세션 배정 타임스탬프(created_at)로 구성되어, 게스트 세션 추적 및 전환 분석 등 업무에 사용됩니다.

필수 필드만 존재해, 개인정보는 외부 시스템에서 별도 관리됩니다.

id.description: 세션 고유 식별자(UUID PK).

actor_type.description: 해당 세션의 사용자 역할 유형 (예: 'admin', 'moderator', 'member', 'guest'). 'discussionboard_auth_sessions.actor_type'에 1:1 대응.

actor_id.description: 역할 소유자(관리자/회원/게스트 등)의 UUID. 외부 tables의 ID 값을 참조합니다.

issued_at.description: 세션이 발급된 시점을 ISO 8601 datetime으로 기록합니다.

oneOf.description: 가장 최근 세션 사용 시각 - 없는 경우 null. 마지막 요청 시마다 갱신됩니다.
가장 최근 세션 사용 시각 - 없는 경우 null. 마지막 요청 시마다 갱신됩니다.

last_activity_at.description: 가장 최근 세션 사용 시각 - 없는 경우 null. 마지막 요청 시마다 갱신됩니다.

oneOf.description: 세션이 취소, 강제종료(로그아웃 등)된 시각. 없으면 null.

IPageIDiscussionboardPosts.description:
A paginated response for searching or listing posts in the discussion board. This is a generic container type used for APIs that return pages of post records as a result of filters, queries, or list operations. Based on the standard IPage<T> container design recommended by the platform.

The data array contains all posts for the current page, and pagination describes how the result relates to the entire data set.

id.description: Primary key of the post record. Unique UUID assigned to each post on creation. Corresponds to the primary key in the schema discussionboard_posts.id.

discussionboard_thread_id.description: Foreign key for the thread this post belongs to. Points to discussionboard_threads.id. Required. Used to group posts within a thread.

discussionboard_member_id.description: Foreign key to the member who authored this post. Points to discussionboard_members.id. This field is always set by server from the authenticated user context. Never settable by clients in creation requests.

oneOf.description: Optional foreign key to the parent post (for comments or replies). Null if the post is a root post, otherwise points to another post in the current thread.
Optional foreign key to the parent post (for comments or replies). Null if the post is a root post, otherwise points to another post in the current thread.

parent_post_id.description: Optional foreign key to the parent post (for comments or replies). Null if the post is a root post, otherwise points to another post in the current thread.

body.description: Main body content for the post. Required string. Arbitrary UTF-8 text.

is_edited.description: Whether this post was edited after initial creation. Used for displaying 'edited' status and for audit/moderation.

is_deleted.description: Soft-deletion flag. true if this post is hidden from normal user view, false otherwise. A soft-deleted post remains in the database for admin/moderator access.

created_at.description: Timestamp for when the post was created, in ISO8601/RFC3339 date-time format.

updated_at.description: Timestamp for last mutation of the post (e.g., edit, soft-delete, or moderation action), in ISO8601/RFC3339 date-time format.

IDiscussionboardPosts.description:
A single post or comment within a thread, as modeled in the discussionboard_posts table. This includes both top-level posts and replies/comments (nested via parent_post_id). Each post consists of an author, potential parent post, content, audit and state metadata, and is timestamped for audit and display.

Sensitive fields (such as password, auth context) are strictly omitted. Only actual schema columns are included.

Complex properties such as permissions are managed by the application, not the data shape.

The parent_post_id field enables the nested comment structure, but is null for top-level posts.

The is_deleted flag is used for soft deletion as required by business and moderation policies.

discussionboard_thread_id.description: Foreign key to the parent thread (discussionboard_threads.id) for the new post. Required for associating the post to a specific thread.

oneOf.description: Optional foreign key for the parent post for replies/comments. Null if making a new root post.
Optional foreign key for the parent post for replies/comments. Null if making a new root post.

parent_post_id.description: Optional foreign key for the parent post for replies/comments. Null if making a new root post.

body.description: Body text for the post. Must be present; checked for length and content validation by backend.

is_edited.description: Should be set to false by default on initial creation, but accepted for up-front setting if required.

IDiscussionboardPosts.ICreate.description:
Request body shape for creating a new discussion board post. Only accepts fields that are required by the Prisma schema or business context:
- discussionboard_thread_id (required)
- parent_post_id (nullable, for replies/comments)
- body (required)
- is_edited (optional, defaults to false if not supplied)

The author/member is always set by the server based on authentication; client must not supply discussionboard_member_id.

is_deleted, created_at, and updated_at are managed server-side and must never be supplied in creation requests.

body.description: If present, the new text body content for the post. May be required based on endpoint; see documentation for which fields are mandatory in update requests.

is_edited.description: If present, declares whether the post is marked as edited as the result of this update action. Set true when performing a real edit; optional.

updated_at.description: Timestamp for when the update occurs (required if the business logic demands client-driven timestamps; otherwise set on backend).

IDiscussionboardPost.IUpdate.description:
Request body shape for updating an existing post. Only fields mutable by the client may appear:
- body (string): new content of the post; typically required, but in some APIs may be optional if only updating other flags
- is_edited (boolean): marks the post as edited
- updated_at (date-time): the timestamp for the update as per backend policy (if permitted)

No support for updating the author, creation date, thread, or id—these must always be immutable or managed by the backend. Never supply is_deleted field; soft-delete is via separate endpoint.
