scenario.draft: Test that a member can update their own post's mutable fields ('body', 'is_edited', 'updated_at'). First, create a user, a thread, and a post. Then perform an update as the owner and verify changes are stored. Attempt to update immutable fields or provide fields not in the schema to confirm validation rejections. Also attempt to update a post as a different member and ensure the API rejects the unauthorized update attempt. Try to update a post that does not exist and verify proper error handling.

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread for post association.
Create a post belonging to the member for authorized updates.
Optionally create a second member profile to test unauthorized update attempts.

scenario.draft: Test soft deletion (by setting is_deleted=true) of a member's own post. First, create a post, then call the delete endpoint and verify is_deleted is set and the post remains in database but is excluded from normal listing if required by spec. Attempt to soft delete a post owned by another member and verify access is forbidden. Attempt to soft delete a non-existent post ID and verify that a suitable error is returned. Also check that deleting a post already marked is_deleted is idempotent or errors appropriately.

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread for post association.
Create a post for soft delete operations.
Optionally create a second member profile to test deletion of posts not owned by the current user.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a paginated list of discussion threads, filtering by category. First, create at least two threads—each in a different discussionboard_category. Then, use this endpoint to query for threads in one specific category with pagination and verify only the relevant thread is returned and pagination metadata is correct. Ensure unrelated threads are excluded from the result set.

dependencies.purpose: Create several threads in different categories to ensure that filtering and pagination provide meaningful and differentiable results. This must be done first to provide actual data for list and filtering tests.
After test thread creation, call this endpoint for category-filtered and paginated retrieval; used to verify business logic for visibility and correct filtering of threads.

scenario.draft: Test listing threads by searching on title keyword. Create a thread with a unique keyword in the title. Then query using the search option for that keyword and verify the thread appears in the response, no unrelated threads are present, and pagination still works as expected.

dependencies.purpose: Set up a thread whose title includes a distinctive keyword, allowing the search feature to be accurately tested.

scenario.draft: Test searching for threads using a filter value that matches no records. Issue a query on the list endpoint for a non-existent combination of category, status, or title. Confirm that the paginated results contain an empty data set and the metadata reflects zero total items.

Test successful retrieval of an individual thread by ID. First, create a thread. Then query this endpoint with the thread's id. Validate that all thread fields match the created data, including title, status, category ID, and other metadata.

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread whose id will then be used to verify successful detail retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test attempting to retrieve a thread with a non-existent id. Call the endpoint with a random or deleted thread id and confirm a not found (404) response is returned.

Test creation of a new discussion thread with valid data. Supply all mandatory fields with correct values, including category ID, title, status, created_at, and confirm a successful response returns the complete thread object as per schema.

Test thread creation with an invalid or non-existent category id. Attempt to create a thread referencing a random or deleted category id. Verify that the operation fails and the error code or message reflects foreign key constraint or invalid reference.

Test successful update of a member's own thread. First, create a thread as the authenticated user, then call this endpoint to update mutable schema fields such as title and status, and verify changes are saved in the response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread owned by the authenticated member that will then be updated. This ensures ownership is properly tested.

scenario.draft: Test update attempt using a non-existent or unauthorized thread id. Call the endpoint with a random or foreign id and expect a not found or forbidden response indicating the user can't update the thread.

Test failure when attempting to update fields not allowed by schema (such as immutable fields like id or created_at). Include these immutable fields in the update payload and confirm that the system rejects the request with corresponding validation errors.

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread so an update can be attempted with forbidden fields, testing business rules enforcement for mutable vs immutable properties.

scenario.draft: Test the soft deletion (archiving) of a member's own thread. Create a thread, then delete it via this endpoint. Afterwards, retrieve the thread and confirm its archived field is set to true and the thread is not included in default list queries.

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread to test the soft delete/archiving process.

scenario.draft: Test attempt to delete (archive) a thread not owned by the authenticated user. Attempt to delete a thread created by another user. System should respond with forbidden or not found error, confirming business logic for ownership enforcement.

Test deleting (archiving) a thread that is already archived. Archive a thread, then attempt to archive it again. Confirm that the endpoint either idempotently returns success or gives a specific error indicating the thread is already archived and cannot be re-archived.

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread, archive it, then attempt to archive again—testing duplicate archival edge case.

scenario.draft: Test a member retrieving their active authentication sessions with valid pagination and filters. The request should retrieve only the sessions linked to the authenticated member, using legitimate filter and sorting criteria on fields like issued_at and status. Validate that pagination and filter options are properly enforced, and that only sessions the member is authorized to view are returned.

Ensure that requesting authentication session list with an invalid filter field (e.g., referencing a non-schema property) results in a validation error. The server must reject any filters or sorts not defined in the discussionboard_auth_sessions schema.

Verify that the authentication session list returned only includes sessions owned by the authenticated member. Pre-create a session for another member and verify this session is never shown to the requesting member, ensuring proper isolation between users' session data.

dependencies.purpose: Create a session for a different member. Required to ensure cross-user isolation.

scenario.draft: Retrieve a single authentication session by its ID and validate that all returned fields match the schema definition. Pre-create a session and attempt to fetch it by its generated ID, confirming all actual session fields (id, actor_type, actor_id, issued_at, expires_at, last_activity_at, revoked_at, ip_address, user_agent) are present in the response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a session to produce a valid id for retrieval.

scenario.draft: Attempt to fetch an authentication session by a non-existent ID and verify that the API returns a not-found error.

Try to retrieve a session which exists but does not belong to the requesting context (e.g., another user's session if permissions are enforced at the session level). Ensure that proper access control is enforced or that the session is simply not found.

dependencies.purpose: Create a session belonging to another user (different actor_id) to verify access restrictions.

scenario.draft: Create a new authentication session with all required fields (actor_type, actor_id, issued_at, expires_at, ip_address, user_agent). Validate that the returned record matches the schema and has properly stored all fields.
Attempt to create a session with one or more required fields omitted. Validate that the API returns appropriate validation errors for each missing field.

Verify that the API does not allow creation of two sessions with the same ID, as IDs must be unique in the schema. Create a session, then attempt to create another session reusing the same id and expect a conflict or validation error.

dependencies.purpose: Create an initial session to produce a duplicate id condition.

scenario.draft: As an authenticated member, update own session record with valid updatable fields (last_activity_at, revoked_at, expires_at, ip_address, user_agent). Ensure only schema fields are mutable and the changes are reflected in the response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a session record for updating during the test.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update an authentication session with a field not present in the schema (e.g., deleted_at). Confirm that the API rejects the update as invalid.

dependencies.purpose: Create a session record to use for invalid update attempts.

scenario.draft: Try to update a session record that does not belong to the authenticated member. Expect a forbidden or not-found error, confirming proper ownership enforcement in session updates.

dependencies.purpose: Create a session record for a different member to test ownership enforcement.

scenario.draft: As an authenticated member, delete own authentication session by id. Validate that the session is permanently removed from the database (no soft-delete) and can no longer be retrieved.

dependencies.purpose: Create a session for the authenticated user in preparation for testing deletion.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete an authentication session which does not belong to the authenticated member. Confirm that the API enforces ownership and responds with an error or not-found, ensuring only own sessions can be deleted.

dependencies.purpose: Create a session for a different member to test access restriction on delete.

scenario.draft: Delete an authentication session, then attempt to delete the same session again to validate that the API properly returns a not-found error for redundant delete attempts.

dependencies.purpose: Create a session, then delete it before re-attempting deletion for error handling check.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a list of poll votes as an admin with advanced filtering, pagination, and sorting options. Ensure results are filtered as expected by poll ID, voting member ID, selected option, and created_at. Validate that only fields present in the schema are filterable. Include tests for both typical filter values (e.g., poll exists with votes, members who have voted) and edge cases (such as filtering results for a non-existent poll or a poll with no votes). Also, confirm paging behavior and ordering of records. Failure scenarios should include unauthorized access attempts by non-admin users and invalid filter criteria (e.g., incorrect field names or types).

dependencies.purpose: Create a poll to ensure there is a valid poll with which votes can be associated.
Create at least one poll vote record for an existing poll, by a member, so that the list endpoint can return non-empty data for valid filters.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving the details of a single poll vote by id as the voting member. Validate that when the poll vote exists and belongs to the requesting member, all schema fields are returned correctly. Confirm appropriate error handling when the vote does not exist or when the requesting member is not the owner (forbidden or not found errors). Include scenarios where the id is malformed or not a UUID. Validate that only authenticated members can access this endpoint.

dependencies.purpose: Create a poll to associate vote entries with a valid poll.
Cast a poll vote as a member and obtain its id for retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving the details of a poll vote by id as a moderator. Ensure all schema fields are accessible, and confirm the vote can be accessed even if not cast by the moderator. Include scenarios for when the poll vote exists and when it does not (expect not found error). Test error conditions such as using an invalid id or attempting access with insufficient permissions. Confirm that the endpoint reflects auditor access for moderation/review, as well as handling pagination if part of a review process.

dependencies.purpose: Create a poll to enable creation of poll votes for review.
Create one or more poll votes to be retrieved by the moderator for audit.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving the details of a poll vote by its id as an admin. Validate correct retrieval of all schema fields when the poll vote exists, and appropriate error responses for non-existent poll vote ids. Include negative cases for invalid id format and ensure correct permission requirements are enforced. This scenario also includes verifying that admin users can access any poll vote for auditing or compliance purposes.

dependencies.purpose: Create a poll for the purposes of associating votes to be audited.
Cast a vote on an active poll to generate a poll vote record for detail retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test creation of a poll vote by an authenticated member on an eligible poll. Success scenario: member votes on an open poll and receives confirmation with all expected schema fields. Failure scenarios: attempting to vote on a closed/expired poll (expect error), voting twice on the same poll (expect unique constraint or duplicate error), submitting an invalid selected_option (violating business constraints), or providing an invalid poll id (not found or foreign key error). Confirmation must be made that the vote is only recorded if all schema and business logic conditions are satisfied. Verify proper authentication enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Create an active poll which will accept votes.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a post history snapshot as an admin by providing a valid post history ID. Ensure the response includes all fields defined by the schema and the correct snapshot data is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post to allow for subsequent editing and history creation.
Edit the post as a member to generate a post history snapshot.

scenario.draft: Test attempting to retrieve a post history snapshot with a non-existent ID. Ensure the API returns a suitable error (such as a 404 Not Found) and the error information is clear in the response.

Test updating the authenticated member's own post history snapshot by ID. Provide valid update data for an allowed field such as edit_reason or edit_type, and verify that the changes are correctly reflected in the returned object. Ownership must be enforced so only the editing member may update their snapshot.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post as a member for editing.
Edit the post to generate a post history snapshot that belongs to the member.

scenario.draft: Test attempting to update a post history snapshot not owned by the authenticated user. The API must reject the request with a forbidden or unauthenticated error, validating strict ownership enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post as Member A.
Have Member A edit the post to create a post history snapshot.
Create a post as Member B to have a different member context for the attempted update.

scenario.draft: Test updating a post history snapshot while attempting to change immutable or non-existent fields (such as id or created_at). The API must reject such updates and return a validation error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post as a member for editing.
Edit the post to generate a post history snapshot.

scenario.draft: Test hard deleting the authenticated member's own post history snapshot by ID. After successful deletion, verify that the snapshot is no longer retrievable and the operation is irreversible.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post to permit creating a post history snapshot.
Edit the post to create a post history snapshot.

scenario.draft: Test attempting to delete a post history snapshot that does not belong to the authenticated member. The API must return a forbidden or unauthorized error, ensuring only owner may delete their snapshot.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post as Member A and generate a post history snapshot.
Create a post as Member B for a different member context (attempt unauthorized delete).

scenario.draft: Test deleting a post history snapshot with a non-existent ID. The API should return a not found error and not affect any other data.

Test retrieving a filtered and paginated list of post edit logs as a member. Apply different filters such as edit_member_id and time ranges, and verify pagination works correctly and returned entries match the filter criteria.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple posts and edits to generate post edit logs.
Edit posts to create log entries.

scenario.draft: Test providing filter criteria that match no post edit logs (such as a random UUID as edit_member_id). The response should return an empty result set but remain a successful request.

Test that a moderator can retrieve, filter, and paginate post edit logs using valid search and sort criteria. Ensure the response contains the correct records and enforces permissions for the moderator role.

dependencies.purpose: Create posts and edits to populate post edit logs.
Edit posts to generate logs before searching as a moderator.

scenario.draft: Test a search as moderator with criteria that will match no records (randomized values). Verify that a valid, but empty, paginated result is returned.

Test that a member can retrieve post history snapshots with a variety of complex filters and pagination options. Verify support for searching by post, by editing member, by edit type, and by created_at time ranges. Create multiple posts and perform multiple edits to generate varied histories first, using different edit types and reasons. Confirm the endpoint supports filtering by post, editor, type, and date accurately, and paginates correctly.

dependencies.purpose: Register members that will be used as post authors and editors.
Create a thread for context.
Create posts in the thread to have post histories attached.
Edit posts to generate post history snapshots for later retrieval.

scenario.draft: Attempt to query the post histories list endpoint without valid authentication or via an unauthorized role, and confirm the request is rejected with an authorization error. This tests secure access.

Test that a moderator can access post history snapshots for moderation purposes. Create content as a member, perform post edits, then as a moderator, query history for specific posts and review edit tracking. Ensure comprehensive edit data is returned in compliance with schema for moderator role. Check filtering by edit_member_id, edit_type, and created_at.

dependencies.purpose: Register both member and moderator accounts.
Create a thread for posts to be edited.
Create posts by members to be edited.
Edit posts to ensure history entries are generated.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin user can list post edit histories using advanced search and filters for compliance/audit review. Populate threads with posts and edits by different members, then as an admin, use all primary filters (post, member, type, date). Ensure returned data matches schema and fulfills admin-level access needs. Test pagination with a large dataset.

dependencies.purpose: Register multiple members for varied history authorship.
Create one or more threads to generate post structures.
Create several posts to seed history.
Perform multiple edits to produce diverse history records.

scenario.draft: Test a member retrieving the full details of their own post edit snapshot using the unique history id. After performing a post edit, fetch its history and verify all returned fields are as expected (id, post reference, edit type, old/new body, etc.).

dependencies.purpose: Register the member.
Create a thread for posts.
Create a post.
Edit the post to generate history.

scenario.draft: Attempt to fetch a post history snapshot by providing an ID that does not exist. Confirm the API returns a proper error response (not found), ensuring error handling for invalid resource access.

Test that a moderator can access the full audit snapshot of any post by its history id. Create posts and make edits as different members, then retrieve the associated edit history as a moderator, confirming field-level access and audit details are present.

dependencies.purpose: Register member and moderator users.
Create a thread for context.
Members create and edit posts to produce histories.
Edit posts and generate history records.

scenario.draft: Test paginated and filtered retrieval of polls as a moderator. This should cover scenarios such as: basic pagination (e.g., retrieving the first/second page), complex filtering (by thread, creator, anonymity, expiration status), and combining sort options (e.g., by most recent or soonest to expire). Ensure that anonymous and non-anonymous polls, expired and active polls, polls created by the requesting moderator and others, and multiple thread associations are properly returned respecting filters. Dependency on the poll creation endpoint is required to ensure test data coverage for all relevant cases.

dependencies.purpose: Create a variety of polls with differing thread associations, anonymity, expiration, creators, and configuration options for pagination and filter testing as a moderator.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a list of polls as an admin including filtering, sorting, and pagination. Coverage should include retrieving all polls, filtering by non-active/expired status, sorting by prompt or expiration, and verifying that admin can see polls across all members and threads regardless of ownership. Validation includes performance for large result sets, correct application of filter and sort criteria as described in business logic.

dependencies.purpose: Set up a large, diverse poll set created by multiple members to ensure admin-level list, filter, and sort tests accurately reflect data spanning multiple users and thread contexts.

scenario.draft: Test viewing detailed poll data as a member. Validate that a member can see details for an existing poll, including prompt, configuration, expiration, and thread association. Also test error cases such as requesting a poll that does not exist (expecting 404) and attempting to access a poll the member is not authorized to see (if such business rules apply). Set up dependencies to create several polls and use both valid and invalid poll IDs in retrieval tests.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least one valid poll to be retrieved by its ID as a member.

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator can retrieve the details of any poll, regardless of ownership, examining fields such as prompt, anonymity, expiration, voting configuration, and creator. Test includes valid retrieval as well as error/edge cases such as non-existent poll ID (should return a 404 error). Ensure that role-based access control allows moderators broader poll visibility than regular members. Dependency: multiple polls with different creators and settings must be established for complete coverage.

dependencies.purpose: Create several polls with diverse configuration, creators, and thread associations to validate moderator's poll retrieval capability and error handling for invalid IDs.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving the details of a ban record by its ID when the record exists. First, create a ban record for a member or guest using the appropriate endpoint. Then, attempt to retrieve the ban using the GET endpoint and verify that all returned fields match the created record's values. This scenario confirms correct data retrieval and field mapping.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new ban record so its ID can be used to test the GET endpoint for existing records.

scenario.draft: Test the system's response when attempting to retrieve a ban record by a non-existent or already-deleted ID. Expect the API to return the appropriate error (e.g., 404 not found), confirming correct handling of missing records and no data leakage occurs for invalid IDs.

Test successful creation of a new permanent ban for a member with all required fields provided and valid values (target member ID, admin ID, valid reason, timestamp, and optional notes). Verify the response contains the correct data and the ban is enforceable via later retrieval endpoints.

Test creating a permanent ban record for a guest, ensuring that only the required guest fields are supplied (guest_id instead of member_id). Confirm the ban appears in subsequent ban list/retrieval operations.

Attempt to create a ban with missing essential fields (e.g., no banned_member_id or banned_guest_id, or no reason). Expect validation to fail and the API to return an error specifying which fields are absent.
Attempt to create a ban for a non-existent member or guest ID. The API should return an error indicating the target does not exist, ensuring integrity of foreign key relationships across entities.

Attempt to create a new ban for a member who already has an active ban. The API should respond with a conflict or business rule error, confirming that duplicate bans for the same target are not allowed (if enforced by the business policy).

dependencies.purpose: First, create an initial ban for the member to establish the precondition for a duplicate ban attempt.

scenario.draft: Test successful update of the reason and notes fields of an existing ban record by an admin. Initially, create a ban record. Then, update its mutable fields and verify the response reflects the changes and no other fields were altered.

dependencies.purpose: Create a ban record to update.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a ban with a non-existent ban ID. The API should return an error indicating that the record was not found, ensuring safe error handling for invalid update attempts.

Attempt to update a valid ban record using credentials of a user without admin rights or who is not the owner. API should reject the operation for insufficient permissions, confirming access control enforcement.

Attempt to update a ban with a payload including invalid or non-schema fields, or setting fields to invalid data types. The API should reject the request with a validation error, ensuring schema compliance is enforced for updates.

dependencies.purpose: Create a ban record to provide a valid ID for testing invalid payloads during update.

scenario.draft: Test successful hard deletion of a ban record by its ID. Create a ban, then delete it via this endpoint. After deletion, verify that the record cannot be retrieved via the GET endpoint, confirming irreversibility.

dependencies.purpose: Create a ban record subject to deletion.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete a ban with an invalid or already-deleted ID. API should return a not found error or similar, confirming correct handling of invalid deletion targets.

Test deletion attempt from a user with insufficient privileges (not an admin or not the creating admin). Verify that access is denied and the record remains unchanged, confirming permission checks are effective.

dependencies.purpose: Create a ban record to set up a valid, restricted deletion scenario.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of post reactions, specifying valid filter criteria such as post ID, member ID, or reaction type. The API should return only matching records, confirming accurate filtering and pagination logic.

dependencies.purpose: Create post reaction records to ensure data exists for filter testing.

scenario.draft: Test querying post reactions with filter parameters that match no records. The API should return an empty paginated result, not an error, confirming correct handling of zero-result searches.
Attempt to retrieve post reactions using invalid filter fields, unsupported data types, or out-of-schema keys. The system should respond with a validation error and not attempt to process the query.

Verify that a member can only retrieve reactions they are authorized to see, depending on their role and ownership. Create reactions as different members and attempt filtering as a non-owner. Confirm the API does not leak data outside the current member’s permissions.

dependencies.purpose: Create post reactions with different members to test data isolation and permission boundaries.

scenario.draft: Verify fetching a specific moderation action by its valid id as a moderator, confirming that all schema fields—id, moderator_id, report_id, affected_post_id, affected_member_id, action_type, action_description, action_timestamp—are returned and correctly populated. This requires first creating a moderation action record and then retrieving it via its id.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation action and obtain the id for retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test the scenario where a moderator attempts to fetch a moderation action that does not exist (invalid/nonexistent id). The system should respond with a not found error and must not leak information about other records or internal state.

Verify that an admin can retrieve the full details of a moderation action by a valid id, ensuring all schema fields are returned and correctly reflect the stored record. Requires creating a moderation action entry and then requesting it as an admin.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation action as admin and obtain the id for detail retrieval.

scenario.draft: Attempt to retrieve a moderation action with an invalid/nonexistent id as an admin and verify that the API returns a not found error, with no record data leak or system failure.

Test successful creation of a moderation action as a moderator by supplying all required schema fields (moderator_id, report_id, affected_post_id, affected_member_id, action_type, action_description, action_timestamp). Validate that the created record can be retrieved and matches the submitted values. This scenario verifies basic creation and storage of moderation actions.

Attempt to create a moderation action as a moderator while omitting one or more required fields (such as action_type or moderator_id). The system should reject the request and return a validation error indicating which field(s) are missing.

Test submission of a moderation action with invalid foreign keys for moderator_id, affected_post_id, affected_member_id, or report_id. The system must return an error for any non-existent references, ensuring referential integrity. This requires knowledge of existing records or the ability to attempt creation with randomly generated (but non-existent) UUIDs.

Verify that an admin can successfully create a moderation action by providing all required schema fields, and that the returned record contains accurate and complete information. The scenario should confirm admin authorization is effective and creation succeeds with proper input.

Attempt to create a moderation action as admin while omitting required fields (such as report_id or action_type). Confirm that the endpoint returns a validation error that clearly specifies the missing fields.

Test that admin attempts to create a moderation action using non-existent foreign key references (e.g., fake moderator_id or affected_post_id) are properly rejected by the system, enforcing referential integrity and error reporting.

Test fetching a specific search history record by its unique searchHistoryId. Begin by creating a search history record for a member using the POST /member//my/searchHistories endpoint, then retrieve it using GET /searchHistories/{searchHistoryId} to ensure all schema fields are returned correctly and the data matches what was inserted.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new search history record and obtain its ID to use for retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a search history record using a non-existent searchHistoryId. Attempt to GET /searchHistories/{searchHistoryId} with a randomly generated UUID that does not exist in the system, and verify that the response correctly returns an error indicating the record was not found.

Test listing search histories for the authenticated member where records exist. First, create multiple search history records using POST /member//my/searchHistories, then call PATCH /member//my/searchHistories with appropriate filter and pagination parameters. Validate that the returned list contains all and only the authenticated member's records, and that records marked as deleted (deleted_at set) are excluded.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple search history records for the authenticated member to ensure test data presence.

scenario.draft: Test listing search histories for an authenticated member who has no search history records (or all are deleted). Authenticate as a member who has not created any search histories, call PATCH /member//my/searchHistories, and verify the paginated result is empty.

Test retrieving a specific search history record for the authenticated member by its searchHistoryId. First, create a new search history record using POST /member//my/searchHistories, then retrieve it using GET /member//my/searchHistories/{searchHistoryId}. Validate that the result includes all schema fields and only records owned by the authenticated member are accessible.

dependencies.purpose: Create a search history record and extract its ID to use for authenticated retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a search history record for an authenticated member using a searchHistoryId belonging to another user. First, create a search history record for a different member, then attempt to retrieve it using another authenticated session and expect a not found or unauthorized error response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a search history record for a different member.

scenario.draft: Test the successful creation of a search history record for the authenticated member. Send a valid payload to POST /member//my/searchHistories and verify that the response includes all the expected schema fields, and the returned data matches the input values appropriately, including correct association with the member ID.

Test failure scenario when attempting to create a search history record with missing required fields. Attempt to POST /member//my/searchHistories while omitting a required property (e.g., search_query) and verify the error response correctly identifies the missing field.

Test the successful update of a search history record owned by the authenticated member. Create a search history record using POST /member//my/searchHistories, then update allowed fields (such as search_query or used_filters) using PUT /member//my/searchHistories/{searchHistoryId}, and confirm that the updated data is reflected in the response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a search history record to update and retrieve its ID.

scenario.draft: Test updating a search history record not owned by the authenticated member. Create a record for one member, then attempt to update it as another member using PUT /member//my/searchHistories/{searchHistoryId}, and validate that a not found or unauthorized error response is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a search history record for a different member to attempt unauthorized update.

scenario.draft: Verify that a moderator can successfully update their own suspension record with valid schema-compliant fields. Use moderator authentication, ensure the targeted suspension record is owned by the authenticated moderator, and update allowed fields such as suspension_reason or suspension_ends_at. Confirm that the returned record reflects the updated values. Prerequisite: a valid suspension record must exist for the moderator.

dependencies.purpose: Create a suspension record that will be updated in this test; must be owned by the authenticated moderator.

scenario.draft: Verify that a moderator cannot update a suspension record not owned by them. Attempt to update the suspension of another moderator and expect an authorization error. This scenario ensures strict ownership enforcement for the /my/ path.

dependencies.purpose: Create a suspension owned by a different moderator for negative test case.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin user can update their own suspension record through the /my/ endpoint, changing allowed fields such as suspension_reason or suspension_ends_at. Ensure the target record belongs to the admin performing the update. Check that changes are applied as expected and no non-schema fields are affected. Prerequisite: a suspension record exists for the admin as the moderator_id.

dependencies.purpose: Create a suspension for the admin to update in this scenario.

scenario.draft: Test that attempts to update non-existent or prohibited fields in a suspension record (such as undefined meta fields) are rejected with proper validation errors. This scenario ensures strong schema validation enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid suspension record for the admin prior to attempted invalid updates.

scenario.draft: Verify that a moderator can successfully perform a hard delete of their own suspension record. Confirm that after deletion, the suspension cannot be retrieved. Ensure only owned suspensions can be deleted using the /my/ path. Prerequisite: create a suspension for the moderator to delete.

dependencies.purpose: Create a suspension for the moderator who will execute the hard delete operation.

scenario.draft: Verify that a moderator cannot delete a suspension record owned by another moderator, and that the API returns the appropriate authorization or forbidden error. This ensures proper enforcement of ownership rules on deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Create a suspension under a different moderator account for negative case testing.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin user can perform a hard delete on their own suspension record, ensuring the record is permanently removed. After deletion, verify the record is not retrievable. Prerequisite: an admin-owned suspension must exist.

dependencies.purpose: Create a suspension record for the admin, to later be deleted in this test.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin cannot delete a suspension not owned by them via the /my/ endpoint, confirming proper authorization enforcement. Attempt deletion of a different user’s suspension and expect an error response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a suspension belonging to a different admin for negative case.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin can successfully retrieve a paginated and filtered list of ban records, filtering on fields such as banned_member_id, banned_guest_id, and is_active. The test should set up multiple ban records, then query with different filtering and pagination options to ensure proper results are returned. Validate that records correspond to query filters and respect schema-only fields.

dependencies.purpose: Create ban records for both members and guests to populate the list and enable meaningful filtering scenarios.

scenario.draft: Verify that filtering the bans list with criteria that match no records results in an empty result set. Set up with known state, then query using filters that do not correspond to any existing ban.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least one ban record for a positive baseline, then query with non-matching filters for the negative case.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can successfully create a new incident report by providing valid values for all required schema fields: incident_code, status, reporter_id, description, created_at. The expected result is a new record in the incident reports table reflecting the provided data. Verify that the returned object contains all schema-defined fields and that business rules regarding enum values for status and required formats are enforced.

Test that attempting to create an incident report without mandatory fields (such as missing incident_code or description) results in a validation error. This ensures that any omitted required schema fields are properly rejected by the API and that a clear error message is returned to the admin user.

Test that when an admin tries to create an incident report using an invalid or unsupported enum value for the status field, the system rejects the request. Ensure that only schema-specified status values are valid and improper values return a validation error.

Test upper-bound length and business validation by submitting an incident report with an extremely long description field. This ensures that the API correctly enforces maximum allowed length and does not allow storage or response truncation or failure.

Test that a moderator can successfully create an incident report using the correct schema fields and that the record is properly associated with their moderator user ID. All required report values (incident_code, status, reporter_id, description, created_at) must be submitted. The result should be a valid incident report tied to the moderator, visible in subsequent queries.

Test case where a moderator attempts to submit two incident reports with the same incident_code (if code is supposed to be unique per system or type). The API should enforce the uniqueness constraint, if applicable, and return an error for the duplicate entry attempt. This verifies enforcement of unique business identifiers within the incident tracking process.

Test retrieving a specific incident report by its ID after it has been created. This validates that the system returns the correct record with all schema fields, accurately reflecting the data stored. Confirm that reading a known existing report returns the precise incident details as submitted.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new incident report to ensure a valid incidentReportId exists for the retrieval test.

scenario.draft: Test attempting to fetch an incident report using a non-existent or malformed incidentReportId (e.g., random UUID, invalid format). The API should return a 404 not found error or a validation error as appropriate, confirming robustness against invalid lookup attempts.

Test that a moderator can successfully retrieve an incident report that was submitted by themselves using the correct incidentReportId. The returned data must match exactly what was submitted, and all schema fields must be present.

dependencies.purpose: Create an incident report as a moderator so the report is available for retrieval by the same role.

scenario.draft: Test the behavior when a moderator attempts to retrieve an incident report with an ID that does not exist. The correct behavior is to return a 404 not found error without exposing unnecessary system or audit information.

Test updating an existing incident report by its ID, changing permitted fields such as status or description, and verifying that the update is correctly persisted in the database. The operation should return the updated incident report with the new values. Only existing schema fields may be changed.

dependencies.purpose: Create a fresh incident report to update, ensuring a valid incidentReportId exists.

scenario.draft: Test updating an incident report and setting the status field to an invalid or unsupported value. The system should reject the update attempt and return a validation error consistent with the schema constraints, confirming strict type enforcement for enums.

dependencies.purpose: Create an incident report to enable an update test for negative enum value scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test the update operation using a non-existent incidentReportId. The system should return a not found error, confirming that only existing reports can be updated and that errors are clear and do not expose system internals.

Test attempting to update an incident report by omitting required fields (if required in PUT requests), to verify whether the system enforces the requirement to provide all necessary update data or can handle partial updates appropriately. The operation should return a validation error if required fields are missing.

dependencies.purpose: Create a sample report to attempt a partial update that omits some schema-mandatory fields.

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated member can retrieve details of a specific post reaction using a valid post reaction ID. The test sets up a post and a post reaction by the member, then requests the reaction details by ID and checks that all expected schema fields are present and correct.

dependencies.purpose: Create a discussion thread for the test post.
Create a post in the created thread. A post is required to react to.
Create a post reaction by the authenticated member for the post.

scenario.draft: Verify that requesting a post reaction by a nonexistent or invalid ID returns a not found or appropriate error. No actual post reaction is created for this test, and a random or deleted ID is used.

Test that a member can successfully create a post reaction. This involves setting up a thread, then a post, and finally submitting a valid reaction to that post. It verifies that a new reaction is recorded and returned according to schema.

dependencies.purpose: Create a discussion thread for the post and reaction.
Create a post in the created thread, which will be reacted to.

scenario.draft: Verify that attempting to create a duplicate reaction (same user, same post, same reaction type) results in a uniqueness/constraint violation error. This test first creates a valid post reaction, then attempts to create an identical reaction by the same member for the same post.

dependencies.purpose: Set up a discussion thread for the test.
Create the post for reaction.
Create the first valid post reaction to be duplicated.

scenario.draft: Test that creating a post reaction with an invalid or non-existent post ID is rejected with an appropriate error indicating the post does not exist.

Verify that the authenticated member can update their own post reaction, changing the reaction type. Precondition: a thread, a post, and a reaction record by the member already exist. The member changes the reaction (e.g., from 'like' to 'love'), and the result should reflect the new reaction type.

dependencies.purpose: Create a discussion thread.
Create a post for reaction.
Record an initial reaction by the member to update.

scenario.draft: Test that a member cannot update a post reaction record they do not own. Set up a post reaction by one member, attempt an update as a different member, and assert that a forbidden or unauthorized error is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread for a post.
Create the post to be reacted to.
Create the reaction as the original owner.
Add a second member for the non-owner update attempt.

scenario.draft: Ensure a member is able to delete their own post reaction. Create a thread, a post, and a reaction by the member, then issue a delete for that reaction and confirm its removal.

dependencies.purpose: Set up a thread for the test.
Create a post in the thread.
Create a reaction that will be deleted by the member.

scenario.draft: Ensure that a member cannot delete a post reaction they do not own. Create the reaction as one member, then attempt to delete as a different member and verify that a forbidden or appropriate error is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread for the test.
Create a post in the thread.
Create a reaction with the first member.
Create a second member to perform the forbidden deletion attempt.

scenario.draft: Verify that a member can retrieve a paginated, filterable list of post likes, specifying filters such as post ID or member ID. Set up multiple posts and likes, then assert that the list endpoint returns correct results according to filters and pagination settings.

dependencies.purpose: Create threads for test posts.
Create multiple posts to be liked.
Create like records on the posts for filter criteria.

scenario.draft: Test the behavior when the list endpoint is called with filter criteria that match no post likes. Set up unrelated data, then request likes with a filter where there should be zero results and assert the empty result set.

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread for an unrelated post.
Create an unrelated post for context.

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator can successfully update a moderation action record owned by themselves using only the schema-allowed fields: action_description, action_type, affected_post_id, affected_member_id, and action_timestamp. Ensure that the updated details are correctly returned in the response, and the changes are accurately reflected in the record. The action id must reference a real moderation action owned by the moderator. Dependencies: the moderator must exist and must have previously created a moderation action with the given id.

dependencies.purpose: Assign moderator role to a member so that the test user has moderator privileges.
Create a moderation action owned by the moderator to set up for update testing.

scenario.draft: Test that updating a moderation action with fields not present in the schema (such as a made-up field or attempt to change the id) is rejected with a validation error. This verifies strict schema adherence and helps prevent data corruption or security issues. Attempt the update with invalid fields and verify the response appropriately rejects the request without changing the stored action data.

dependencies.purpose: Assign moderator role so the test user is authorized.
Create a valid moderation action record for testing invalid field update.

scenario.draft: Verify that attempting to update a moderation action not owned by the authenticated moderator (i.e., another moderator's record) is rejected due to permission checks. The scenario requires at least two moderator users: one creates a moderation action, the other attempts to update it and should receive a forbidden or not-authorized error response. This enforces business rules around action ownership and data privacy.

dependencies.purpose: Assign moderator roles to two members to simulate multiple moderators.
Create a moderation action with the first moderator for update attempts with the second.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can successfully update one of their own moderation action records by id, modifying only schema-allowed fields such as action_description, action_type, affected_post_id, affected_member_id, and action_timestamp. Verify that the update is persisted and response contains updated data. Admin must first create a moderation action for themselves to enable this test.

dependencies.purpose: Assign admin role so the test user has admin privileges.
Create a moderation action owned by the admin user to be updated in this scenario.

scenario.draft: Test that attempting to update a moderation action with undocumented or schema-forbidden fields (such as adding fields not defined or trying to change the id) results in validation errors, and the underlying record is not affected. This ensures the admin endpoint enforces schema correctness.

dependencies.purpose: Assign admin role so the test user has admin privileges.
Create a moderation action owned by the admin for update with invalid fields test.

scenario.draft: Ensure that if an admin tries to update a moderation action record not owned by them (i.e., created by another admin or moderator), the attempt results in a forbidden or not-authorized error response. This scenario enforces update permission boundaries between admins. Requires two admin users for full test coverage.

dependencies.purpose: Assign admin roles to two distinct users to simulate two admin accounts.
First admin creates moderation action; second admin attempts the update.

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator can successfully delete (hard-delete) their own moderation action record by id. The record is permanently removed from the system with no recovery possible, and confirm the action cannot be found after deletion. The moderator must have an existing moderation action before performing the delete.

dependencies.purpose: Assign moderator role to a member for proper permissions.
Create a moderation action record for the moderator to enable testing deletion.

scenario.draft: Verify that attempting to delete a moderation action not owned by the current moderator (i.e., one created by another moderator) results in a forbidden or not-authorized error. This test upholds data ownership integrity. Involves two moderator users: one creates the record, the other attempts deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Create two moderator users with the appropriate role assignment.
Have one moderator create an action so the other can attempt deletion.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can hard-delete one of their own moderation action records by id. Once the operation is completed, the record must not be retrievable. The admin should first have created a moderation action record for this test.

dependencies.purpose: Assign admin privileges to the test user.
Create a moderation action record owned by the admin to test deletion.

scenario.draft: Test that trying to delete a moderation action created by another admin or moderator using the current admin's credentials fails due to permission enforcement. This requires preparing two distinct admin users and demonstrating that one cannot delete the other's actions.

dependencies.purpose: Assign admin roles to two users for permission boundary checks.
One admin creates a moderation action; the other attempts unauthorized deletion.

scenario.draft: Test the retrieval of a paginated and filtered list of warning logs issued by moderators to members. Provide different search and filter options (e.g., by moderator_id, warned_member_id, reason substring, issued_at range, or sorted by issued_at) in the request body, and verify that only matching warning logs are returned with correct pagination information. This scenario checks business logic for moderation log visibility and list accuracy. Assumes there are multiple warning logs in the system for a comprehensive query test.

dependencies.purpose: Assign moderator role so the test user can create warning logs.
Create several warning logs with different fields to populate data for list/filter testing.

scenario.draft: Test that providing a filter which does not match any existing warning log (for example, a non-existent warned_member_id or a reason string not present in any entry) results in an empty list being returned. This scenario ensures correct handling of no-result cases without errors. This is important for UX and API predictability.

dependencies.purpose: Assign moderator role so the test user can create warning logs.
Create at least one warning log to ensure the table is not empty, then filter with a value that cannot match.

scenario.draft: Test that an unauthorized or non-moderator user cannot retrieve the list of warning logs, resulting in an authorization error. Attempt to access the endpoint with a user lacking moderator or admin rights, and verify the response enforces proper authorization policies. This validates security and compliance measures around moderation log access.

dependencies.purpose: Create a regular member without moderator/admin rights for negative access test.

scenario.draft: Verify that an administrator can successfully hard-delete an existing platform policy record by its unique ID. First, create a new platform policy using POST /policyAudit/platformPolicies to ensure there is a policy to delete. Then, delete that policy with DELETE /policyAudit/platformPolicies/{platformPolicyId} and confirm the operation succeeds (e.g., 204 No Content or deletion confirmation) and that GET /policyAudit/platformPolicies/{platformPolicyId} for the same ID after deletion returns a not found error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a platform policy to ensure a valid record exists for deletion.
Verify that record creation and subsequent deletion are reflected in retrievable detail before and not found after.

scenario.draft: Verify that attempting to delete a non-existent platform policy ID as an administrator results in a 404 not found or similar error. Attempt the DELETE operation with a randomly generated UUID that does not match any existing platform policy record and assert that the API responds with the appropriate error response, confirming safe handling of unknown IDs.

Test the retrieval of a paginated and filtered list of audit logs as an admin. The scenario should include:
- Using no filters to get a default paginated list.
- Applying filters for action_type, actor_id, or created_at range to ensure filtering works as intended.
- Verifying results are paginated and can be sorted as specified in the request body, and that results contain only schema-specified fields (id, action_type, description, actor_id, target_id, created_at).
- Ensuring that only authorized admin users can access this endpoint, while unauthorized users are denied access.

Verify that querying the audit log list with filter criteria that yield no results (such as an impossible actor_id or future time range) returns a valid paginated response with an empty list but no errors. This ensures the API gracefully handles empty result sets.

Verify the retrieval of a single audit log entry by its valid unique ID as an admin. First, perform or simulate an action that generates an audit log entry (such as creating a new policy, which should be logged if audit triggers are active). Then, retrieve the audit log by its ID and assert that the returned data matches the schema and that all required fields are present and accurate.

dependencies.purpose: Generate an auditable action by creating a platform policy, assuming this action is logged.
List audit logs to extract the ID of a recently created log entry for detail retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test the behavior when an admin attempts to fetch details of a non-existent audit log record using a random UUID. The endpoint should respond with a 404 or appropriate error, confirming secure no-leakage behavior for invalid IDs.

Verify admin retrieval of a list of incident reports with various filter and pagination options. The test should include:
- Requesting all incident reports with no filters for a default page.
- Using filters for specific status, incident_code, reporter_id, description keywords, or created_at ranges, verifying only matching records are returned.
- Testing pagination parameters to ensure results can be paged through correctly and fields match the schema only.

Submit a search with filters that cannot possibly match any incident reports (such as a random incident_code or a time range in the far future) to verify that the response is a valid page with an empty results array and does not return errors, confirming correct empty state behavior.
Attempt to access this endpoint with a non-admin, non-moderator account and assert that access is denied (401/403), confirming correct role-enforcement for sensitive incident data.

Verify that a user with moderator privileges can retrieve incident reports with filters or pagination, mirroring admin access but using a moderator session. Ensure all filtering, sorting, and pagination is reflected as described in the admin test, including schema-only field validation.

Use edge case filters with the PATCH body (such as start date in the far past, unusual status values, or large page sizes) and verify API stability and schema-compliance of results. Ensure the API does not crash, that empty or large result sets are handled correctly, and that invalid filter values trigger validation errors where applicable.

Attempt to list incident reports using a malformed or revoked session as a moderator and confirm the endpoint returns the appropriate unauthorized or session-expired error, preserving security for incident report data.

Test a successful update of an incident report by a moderator. First, create a new incident report using correct schema fields as a moderator. Then, attempt to update allowed fields (incident_code, status, reporter_id, description, updated_at) on this record. Ensure the response reflects the new values and only permits changes to fields within the schema. Ownership and permission enforcement should be validated so that only authorized moderators can update.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new incident report as a prerequisite so that an existing report is available to update.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update an incident report using an incidentReportId that does not exist. The system should return a not found error. Validate correct error handling for non-existent records and ensure no fields are mutated.

Test updating an incident report by including fields not present in the schema. The request should be rejected, and the API must return a validation error specifying the misuse of invalid properties. Confirm no update occurs and only schema-compliant fields are allowed.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid incident report before attempting an invalid update.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update an incident report as an unauthorized user (e.g., as a member or guest instead of a moderator/admin). The API should return an unauthorized or forbidden error, preventing the operation.

dependencies.purpose: Create an incident report as a moderator so it exists to test improper permission for update.

scenario.draft: Test successful hard deletion of an incident report by an admin. First, create a new incident report (using moderator or admin privilege), then delete it using the admin route. Confirm the record is irreversibly removed and cannot be retrieved afterward. Validate correct permissions and permanent deletion behavior.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new incident report so that an existing record is available for deletion.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete an incident report with a non-existent incidentReportId. Confirm that a not found error is returned and that no records are removed.
Attempt to perform deletion as a user who is not an admin (such as a member or moderator lacking proper access). The system should return a forbidden error and not execute any deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Create an incident report with admin privilege to test deletion with insufficient permission.

scenario.draft: Test successful hard deletion of an incident report by a moderator. First, a moderator creates a new incident report. Then, the report is deleted using the moderator endpoint. After deletion, attempts to retrieve the incident report should fail, confirming it was irreversibly removed.

dependencies.purpose: Set up a valid incident report entry to be deleted during the test.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete an incident report as an unauthorized actor (such as a member or guest). The request should be rejected with a forbidden error. Validate that only moderators and admins can perform this operation.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid incident report to ensure there is a record for unauthorized users to attempt to delete.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete an incident report using a randomly generated UUID that does not correspond to any existing record. Confirm that the API returns a not found error and does not remove any data.

Test listing and searching appeals as an admin using a variety of search, filter, and pagination criteria. The test should cover filtering by status, outcome, appellant_id, and created_at date ranges, as defined in the schema. Also, check that sorting and pagination work properly. Validate that only appeals matching the query are returned and others are excluded.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple appeals with diverse data to ensure there are enough entries to test filtering and pagination as an admin.

scenario.draft: Test searching for appeals as an admin using filter criteria that match no records. Confirm that the system returns an empty result set and no errors are raised.

Attempt to use the PATCH /admin/policyAudit/appeals endpoint as an unauthorized role (e.g., member or guest). Confirm the API returns a forbidden error, ensuring only admins and moderators can access this route.

Test listing and searching appeals records as a moderator, using filters such as status, appellant_id, incident_id, and created_at range. Confirm that only records matching the query are returned and pagination/sorting features act as expected. Coverage should affirm retrieval of only permitted data for the moderator role.

dependencies.purpose: Set up multiple appeal records with varied data so there are sufficient examples for searching and filtering as a moderator.

scenario.draft: Test searching for appeals as a moderator using criteria that do not match any entries. Validate that an empty result set is provided, and pagination metadata are correct.
Attempt to use the PATCH /moderator/policyAudit/appeals endpoint as a role lacking moderator privileges (e.g., member, guest). The API should return a forbidden error and prevent access.

Verify that an authenticated member can successfully retrieve the details of a mention they own by its unique ID. First, create a member, then create a post, and create a mention referencing this member in the post. Use the resulting mention's ID to fetch the mention. Check that all predefined schema fields are present in the response and match what was created.

dependencies.purpose: Create a mention to obtain a valid mention ID for retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test behavior when trying to retrieve a mention by an ID that does not exist. Attempt to fetch a mention with a random/non-existent UUID as the ID and verify that the system returns a suitable not found error response.

Verify that a member cannot retrieve details of a mention they do not own (i.e., their member ID does not match mentioned_member_id). Setup: register two members, create a post, and then create a mention for member1 where only member2 is authenticated during GET. Expect a forbidden or not found error, depending on business logic.

dependencies.purpose: Create a mention assigned to a different member to test access control.

scenario.draft: Validate that an authenticated member can create a new mention by supplying a valid post and mentioned member. Setup: Create two members and a post, then create a mention linking the post to the second member. Check for successful creation and response fields compliance with schema.
Check that creating a mention with a non-existent post ID fails with an appropriate error due to foreign key violation. Try to use a random or invalid post UUID and verify error.

Ensure creation fails if the mentioned_member_id does not correspond to an existing member. Attempt to create a mention using a non-existent member UUID and expect a clear error indicating foreign key constraint failure.

Attempt to create a mention while not authenticated (guest or logged out user). Verify that the system blocks the request with an appropriate authorization error since only authenticated members may create mentions.

Confirm that an authenticated member can update their own mention entry, changing either the parent post or the mentioned_member_id to another valid entity. Setup: Register two members, create two posts, and a mention. Attempt to change the mention to refer to the second member or another post, and verify successful update and schema correctness.

dependencies.purpose: Create an initial mention to perform the update operation.

scenario.draft: Test the failure case where a member tries to update an owned mention to reference a non-existent post. Expect an error indicating foreign key violation.

dependencies.purpose: Create an initial mention to perform the update operation.

scenario.draft: Try to update a mention owned by another member. Setup: create member1 and member2; member1 creates a mention; member2 attempts to update it using the same ID. The system should reject the request with a forbidden error, enforcing record ownership.

dependencies.purpose: Create the mention owned by member1 to test forbidden access for member2.

scenario.draft: Confirm that a member can successfully hard-delete a mention record they own, removing it from the system. Setup: Create a member and a mention, then perform the DELETE with authentication. Verify that the mention is no longer retrievable afterward and cannot be recovered.

dependencies.purpose: Create a mention to obtain an ID for deletion.

scenario.draft: Validate that attempting to delete a mention not owned by the member fails with a forbidden or not found error, thus enforcing row-level data access control.

dependencies.purpose: Create the mention as a different member to test forbidden delete.

scenario.draft: Test that an authenticated member receives a paginated and filterable list of their own notifications. Setup: Register a member and create several notifications for them, then list with/without various filter or pagination settings. Verify response correctness, ownership enforcement, and pagination compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Create notifications for the test member in batch, to prepare data for retrieval.

scenario.draft: Check that advanced filtering and searching parameters (e.g., filtering by notification type, opened status, or title) are honored in the list results. Setup: Create multiple notifications with different values for searchable fields, then test search and filter capabilities, verifying only matching notifications are returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create notifications with various filterable attributes for testing advanced list options.

scenario.draft: Validate that notifications soft-deleted (deleted_at set) are not returned in the list of active notifications. Setup: Create notifications, soft-delete some using the DELETE operation, then fetch and check that only non-deleted notifications appear in the result.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple notifications and soft-delete some via DELETE to test filtering of deleted records.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of platform policies with different filters, sorting, and pagination options as an admin. Ensure that filtering by title, policy_code, is_active, and sorting by published_at/updated_at works correctly. Scenario covers: (1) default/all records, (2) filter by title substring, (3) filter by is_active=false, (4) sorting by updated_at descending, (5) pagination boundaries (first/last page), and (6) requesting with empty or invalid filter keys. Expect only actual schema fields in results, no extra or missing properties. If schema fields do not exist or filters are invalid, backend should ignore or raise a validation error. Only policies accessible by admin role should be returned. No dependency on specific data creation but relies on having at least several policies in the system to test effective filtering and paging behaviors.

dependencies.purpose: Create several platform policy records with varying titles, codes, active statuses, and published_at dates to ensure the list operation can be meaningfully tested against diverse data.

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of a new platform policy by an admin. Supply all required fields with valid data: policy_code (unique), title, policy_text, is_active. Confirm that the API returns the complete newly created record with all schema fields correctly set, and that published_at and updated_at are automatically handled by the server. Verify that the new policy can be retrieved via GET /policyAudit/platformPolicies/{platformPolicyId}.

Test failure scenario when attempting to create a platform policy with a policy_code that already exists. Attempt to create two policies with the same policy_code and different titles. System should reject the second attempt, enforcing unique constraint on policy_code and returning a conflict or validation error response. This checks proper business rule enforcement for uniqueness.

dependencies.purpose: Create the first platform policy with a unique policy_code to establish the precondition for a duplicate attempt.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of a single platform policy by its ID as an admin. Start by creating a policy, then fetch it using its returned id. Validate that all returned fields exactly match the schema, and the id, code, and text match what was submitted. If the id does not exist, the system must return a not-found error. Check that only users with admin role may access this endpoint.

dependencies.purpose: Create a platform policy to retrieve, so the platformPolicyId is valid.

scenario.draft: Test the behavior when an admin tries to fetch a platform policy with an ID that does not exist in the system. Ensure a proper not-found (404) error is returned, and that the system does not leak any data about other records. This validates correct error handling for invalid lookups.

Test successful update of an existing platform policy by an admin. Update mutable fields such as policy_text, title, or is_active, using the id of an existing policy. Verify that the response contains updated values, no changes to immutable fields, and that a subsequent GET reflects the new data. Only schema fields should be in input and output. Updates to is_active and policy_text should persist as stored.

dependencies.purpose: Create a policy to update, establishing a valid platformPolicyId.

scenario.draft: Test the behavior when updating a platform policy by an invalid/nonexistent platformPolicyId. Attempt the update as admin and verify a not-found (404) is returned, and that no other records are affected by the request.

Test authorization by simulating a non-admin user attempting to update a policy via this endpoint. Attempt a valid update payload as a user with insufficient privileges (e.g., member role), expect an access denied error. Policy should not change in system.

dependencies.purpose: Create a policy as admin for update attempt.

scenario.draft: Test successful hard deletion of a business rule by an admin. Create a business rule, then delete it via its id. Confirm the record is permanently removed and cannot be retrieved via GET afterward. Test validates compliance with hard delete, not soft delete, as the schema supports only direct removal.

dependencies.purpose: Create a business rule to obtain a valid businessRuleId for deletion test.

scenario.draft: Test hard delete request for a business rule with an invalid or randomly generated businessRuleId. Ensure system responds with a not-found (404) and does not remove or reveal any other records.

Attempt to delete an existing business rule using a user with insufficient authorization (e.g., member or moderator role). The request must be rejected with an access denied error, and the rule should remain untouched.

dependencies.purpose: Create a business rule as admin, then test unauthorized deletion attempt.

scenario.draft: Test successful retrieval of a notification by its notificationId for an authenticated member. First, create a member and a notification assigned to this member. Then, retrieve the notification by its ID and verify all notification fields are returned, the ID matches, and ownership is correct.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member to represent the authenticated user who will receive notifications.
Create a new notification belonging to the registered member that can be retrieved in this scenario.

scenario.draft: Test error handling when attempting to retrieve a notification by an ID that does not exist or is not owned by the authenticated member. Attempt to fetch a notification using a random UUID that has not been assigned or one that belongs to another member, and verify that an appropriate error (not found or forbidden) is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Register two test members for permission testing or error simulation.
Create a notification for the first member; use an unrelated ID for the not-found and forbidden tests.

scenario.draft: Test creating a new notification for the authenticated member with valid required fields. After registering a member, use the endpoint to create a notification with proper type, title, and body fields. Verify the returned notification contains all expected schema fields, the owner matches the member, and values match the request.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member who will be the authenticated user/owner of the notification.

scenario.draft: Test error handling when required fields are missing or invalid in the notification creation request. Attempt to create a notification for the member with omitted type or title field and verify that a validation error response is received, confirming correct enforcement of schema requirements.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member who will be the test owner for the notification creation attempt.

scenario.draft: Test updating a notification belonging to the authenticated member. Register a member, create a notification for them, and then update fields such as title, body, or opened flag. Verify that the returned notification reflects the updated values and that non-updatable fields remain unchanged.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to act as the authenticated user.
Create a notification owned by the member that will be updated in this scenario.
